title: Prediction Markets Never Bought Trump’s Dana White Press Secretary Pick
summary: President Donald Trump surprised political observers with his Saturday announcement that he had offered the White House press secretary job to UFC CEO Dana White. After a few thin opening trades, Kalshi and Polymarket traders priced White’s chances of becoming press secretary below 20% for almost th...
content:
President Donald Trump surprised political observers with his Saturday announcement that he had offered the White House press secretary job to UFC CEO Dana White. After a few thin opening trades, Kalshi and Polymarket traders priced White’s chances of becoming press secretary below 20% for almost the entire weekend, and his odds fell to 1 to 2 cents after Trump said on Sunday he had been kidding.

Key Takeaways

  • Kalshi’s Dana White contract stayed below 20 cents after a thin, volatile first 13 minutes of trading.
  • Polymarket’s White contract topped out at 15 cents, and most of its largest trades bet against him.
  • Both fell to 1-2 cents after Trump said on Sunday that the offer was a joke.

Trump Offers White the Job, Then Says He Was Kidding

“I am pleased to announce that the great Dana White, a violent fighter and warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Saturday, asking White to bring several UFC fighters as “assistants” to defend against the “Lunatic Left.”

The job has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left in October after five days, and Trump’s post came a day after he replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in the Nov. 3 midterms.

White posted an apparently AI-generated image of himself at the briefing room podium to his Instagram story, captioned “On to the next chapter,” and said at a boxing news conference in London that he was flying to Washington to meet Trump on Monday. CNN reported on Saturday, citing a source familiar with the matter, that White had declined the offer.

On Sunday evening U.S. Eastern time, Trump said he had been joking about the matter.

“I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea,” he told reporters in Palm Beach, Florida, according to NBC News. He said Monday’s meeting with White was still on, but “for other reasons.”

Kalshi Traders Priced White Below 20 Cents

Kalshi added Dana White to its next press secretary market at 19:12 UTC on Saturday. Its first, thinly traded minutes ranged from 3 to 58 cents, including 142 contracts at up to 58 cents at about 19:19 UTC, but the price was 18 cents by 19:22 UTC and 7 cents by 19:35 UTC.

For the rest of Saturday, White’s contract traded between 1 and 18 cents, with brief rises to 18 cents at about 20:57 UTC and 16 cents at 21:40 UTC, before sliding back to single digits. On Sunday, it mostly traded at 4 to 6 cents, before dropping to 1 to 2 cents between 23:24 and 23:27 UTC, around the time Trump said he had been joking. About 3.16 million contracts have changed hands, roughly 94% of them at prices under 10 cents.

Kalshi also listed side markets. One, on whether White would publicly decline the job before Nov. 8, settled “No.” A second, with a Nov. 10 deadline, was trading at 32 cents on Monday, while a market on whether White would visit the White House before Nov. 10 stood at 80 cents.

Polymarket Bettors Bet Against White

Polymarket opened a Dana White contract in its next press secretary event at 19:41 UTC on Saturday, and it saw its first trade at 19:44 UTC. Its highest trade was 15 cents, at 20:26 UTC, and it traded near 5 cents on Sunday and around 2 cents on Monday. The contract resolves “Yes” only if the White House announces that White has been picked.

About $70,000 has changed hands in 398 trades on the contract. Seven of its eight largest trades were purchases of “No” shares, betting that White would not get the job, led by a $7,732 buy at almost 99 cents at 01:54 UTC on Monday.

At the time of writing, neither platform has a clear favorite for the job. On Kalshi, Danielle Alvarez and Anna Kelly led at 17 and 16 cents on Monday, while Polymarket had Kelly in front at 13 cents. Insider trading on White House-related markets has drawn regulators’ attention before: a former White House teleprompter operator was ordered to pay $172,539 over Kalshi bets on Trump’s speeches.

title: Bitso Business Says Stablecoin Payment Volume Now Runs Above $150B Annualized
summary: Bitso Business says the payment flows passing through its infrastructure have reached an annualized rate above $150 billion, up 83% from $82 billion a year earlier. The November 4 disclosure puts Latin American cross-border payments back in focus…
content:
TL;DR: Bitso Business says the payment flows passing through its infrastructure have reached an annualized rate above $150 billion, up 83% from $82 billion a year earlier. The November 4 disclosure puts Latin American cross-border payments back in focus as a practical use for stablecoins.

Bitso Business says the payment flows passing through its infrastructure have reached an annualized rate above $150 billion, up 83% from $82 billion a year earlier. The November 4 disclosure puts Latin American cross-border payments back in focus as a practical use for stablecoins. The number is significant, but it describes an annualized transaction run rate, not net revenue, assets under custody or a full calendar year's independently audited settlement.

How to read the number

Bitso estimates the annualized total payment volume equates to more than $410 million a day, and says more than 2,000 institutional clients use its infrastructure. Annualization converts a recent rate into a twelve-month equivalent; the actual figure realized over a full year may differ if activity changes. Payment volume also counts money passing through the system, potentially more than once, rather than money earned by the company. That distinction matters when comparing Bitso with businesses reporting fees or profit. The rate is a company-provided operating metric and deserves to be followed across subsequent periods.

Why stablecoins are involved

Cross-border transfers often require businesses to move between banking networks, local currencies and different operating hours. Stablecoin liquidity can act as one route for transferring value between institutions that otherwise face cutoffs or slow intermediaries. Bitso's model seeks to join local payment systems to that round-the-clock settlement layer. It does not mean every end customer receives or holds a stablecoin. In many implementations, the customer sees a familiar local-currency payment while a service provider manages the conversion and digital asset transfer in the background.

Where the economic benefit comes from

The promised advantages are faster availability, predictable reconciliation and the ability to process transfers outside normal banking hours. Whether customers actually save money depends on exchange spreads, local partner fees, liquidity and compliance costs. Businesses also need reliable offramps, because payment utility often ends with a local bank balance rather than an onchain token. Stablecoins do not abolish capital controls or national payment laws. They add another settlement mechanism that must work with those requirements. That is why regional partnerships and regulated access can be as valuable as the underlying blockchain.

Latin America's specific demand

Remittances, business-to-business payments and cross-border commerce create frequent currency conversion needs across the region. Bitso identifies remittance businesses, neobanks, payments firms and digital commerce among its institutional customers. These use cases can be less speculative than trading crypto solely for a price gain. Still, volume growth can reflect more customers, faster recycling of existing capital or changes in foreign exchange conditions. A rising total does not independently show how many households benefited, the average cost per transaction or the distribution of volume by country.

What would demonstrate durable scale

Future reporting should clarify transaction count, recurring client retention, settlement costs and the proportion of payments completed successfully within target times. Transparency about counterparty, issuer and local currency risks would also help. The development shows how stablecoins may be embedded in everyday financial operations, but the practical success is measured by reliable money movement, not by the number of tokens circulating on a particular chain.

Primary source: Bitso Business company announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s coverage of another consumer-facing stablecoin payment rollout.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: XRP Ledger Foundation Offers $40K to Teach XRPL and Its Next Upgrades
summary: The XRP Ledger Foundation offered up to $40,000 for educational content about the network and proposed upgrades. Its Education Month campaign accepts videos, tutorials, articles, and other formats, with fact-checking required before awards. Foundation Launches XRP Ledger Education Month The XRP Ledg...
content:
The XRP Ledger Foundation offered up to $40,000 for educational content about the network and proposed upgrades. Its Education Month campaign accepts videos, tutorials, articles, and other formats, with fact-checking required before awards.

Key Takeaways

  • Creators can explain proposed upgrades, existing features, and protocol principles.
  • Eligible formats include videos, tutorials, articles, art, and graphics.
  • The foundation checks facts before awards, with payment after a signed agreement.

Foundation Launches XRP Ledger Education Month

The XRP Ledger Foundation shared the launch of XRP Ledger Education Month on X on Nov. 9, offering up to $40,000 in awards for educational content. In its education campaign announcement, the foundation stated:

“Up to $40,000 in awards for educators and content creators who explain upcoming amendments like the Lending Protocol, or teach how the XRP Ledger works, the role of XRP and the core protocol philosophies.”

Suggested subjects include the Lending Protocol, Confidential Transfers, consensus, issued assets, NFTs, XRP’s role, and protocol design. NFTs, or nonfungible tokens, represent unique assets. The foundation invited creators to choose the topic they were most passionate about.

The initiative aligns with the foundation’s community and protocol development work, which includes infrastructure, technical standards, and long-term ecosystem development. The organization describes its mission as keeping the ledger open, transparent, and accessible.

Creators Choose Formats as Foundation Checks Facts

Accepted formats include videos and shorts, explainer series, tutorials, articles and threads, art and animation, and graphics. The campaign encouraged creators to explain the XRP Ledger in their own style. Submission instructions called for tagging @XRPLF on X or adding #XRPEducationMonth on YouTube, TikTok, or elsewhere.

Entries should be understandable without a technical background, accurate, creative, and consistent, with material people could learn from and share. The foundation said it would check facts before any award, while its criteria also favored an individual style and repeated participation. Once the submission window closes, it will select the work to receive awards, with payments following a signed agreement.

Proposed Upgrades Give Creators More Topics to Explain

The campaign identified the Lending Protocol and Confidential Transfers as subjects for educational content about upcoming amendments. These topics would let creators explain what the proposed features do and what they are for. Both appeared alongside broader subjects such as consensus, issued assets, NFTs, and protocol design.

The proposed Lending Protocol remained subject to validator approval as of Nov. 9 and would support fixed-term, uncollateralized loans using funds pooled in single-asset vaults. Borrowers’ ability to repay would be assessed outside the blockchain, while the ledger would record loan terms and administer repayments. A loan broker could contribute first-loss capital, using its own funds to absorb an initial portion of default losses.

Confidential Transfers would shield balances and transfer amounts for certain issued tokens while retaining mechanisms for authorized parties to verify information. Existing network features offered another route for participation, including explanations of how consensus works and how issued assets and NFTs operate. The foundation’s instructions allowed contributors to choose among these subjects and present them through their preferred teaching format.

title: OpenAI builds kill switch to stop rogue agents within 35 seconds
summary: Control Room cuts off model output for internal research jobs when people or automated monitors flag safety or security concerns.
content:
OpenAI has built a system that can cut off an AI research experiment’s access to model output, following several disclosures of its models acting beyond their instructions this year.

In a blog post Monday, OpenAI called the system “Control Room,” which is a centralized system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and stops them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

“As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” said the company.

The announcement comes after OpenAI disclosed several incidents this year in which research models acted outside their instructions during evaluations. In July, the company said its models had escaped a restricted testing environment and hacked Hugging Face to cheat on a security evaluation.

In October, it disclosed that a research model had used a crypto wallet without authorization to pay for smart contract deployments using testnet Ether, then omitted the spending from its final summary.

Control Room currently covers OpenAI’s internal research workloads, such as training experiments, evaluations and data processing.

It works by assigning each research job an identifier, which the inference engine checks before generating model output. If a person or automated monitoring system orders the job stopped, Control Room revokes its authorization, blocking further output even if the underlying research program keeps running, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI said cached authorizations could delay a shutdown by up to 35 seconds. The system is also designed to reject new requests if Control Room becomes unavailable.

Related: DeepSeek developing AI agent requiring less human input: Report

title: EDX Markets Adds Bitcoin-Backed CBTC Trading for Canton Institutions
summary: EDX Markets says it has partnered with BitSafe to introduce spot trading in CBTC, a Bitcoin-backed asset built for the Canton Network. The November 5 announcement describes the token's first centralized-exchange listing and an institutional…
content:
TL;DR: EDX Markets says it has partnered with BitSafe to introduce spot trading in CBTC, a Bitcoin-backed asset built for the Canton Network. The November 5 announcement describes the token's first centralized-exchange listing and an institutional marketplace where eligible clients can trade CBTC against US dollars.

EDX Markets says it has partnered with BitSafe to introduce spot trading in CBTC, a Bitcoin-backed asset built for the Canton Network. The November 5 announcement describes the token's first centralized-exchange listing and an institutional marketplace where eligible clients can trade CBTC against US dollars. This is not a new version of native Bitcoin; it is a separate representation intended to make Bitcoin exposure usable inside Canton's financial ecosystem.

What CBTC is designed to represent

According to EDX and BitSafe, each CBTC is backed one-for-one by Bitcoin. The asset is intended to support activities such as trading, lending and transfers in a privacy-enabled institutional environment. The partners point to distributed reserve controls and Chainlink Proof of Reserve as safeguards around backing. Those features are important, but a proof-of-reserve feed is not necessarily a complete audit of liabilities, ownership or redemption processes. Institutions still need to review custody agreements, redemption rights, legal claims and the conditions under which a token can be exchanged for its backing.

Why an exchange listing matters

An asset created for use on an institutional chain needs reliable ways for participants to enter and exit positions. A trading pair against dollars can provide a price-discovery venue and simplify access for eligible institutions. Yet listing is not the same as deep liquidity. Effective markets require active market makers, transparent execution, operational reliability and practical transfer arrangements between the exchange and the Canton network. The announcement does not establish a certain future daily volume or demonstrate that every Canton participant will automatically have access to the product.

Wrapped Bitcoin comes with different risks

Native BTC settles on Bitcoin's own ledger under its network rules. A Bitcoin-backed token requires additional trust in the issuer, custodian, reserve accounting and any smart contracts or permissions used to control transfers. An institution may accept those conditions to obtain functionality it cannot easily achieve with native BTC. But the distinction must remain visible in both product descriptions and risk controls. A one-for-one target does not guarantee that a token trades at parity in every market condition, especially if redemptions are delayed or access is restricted.

Canton's institutional design shapes the use case

Canton aims to connect financial applications while giving participating organizations control over sensitive information. A Bitcoin-backed asset could make collateral or financing arrangements easier within that environment, but it must integrate with the controls required by institutions. That might mean identity verification, permissioned counterparties and restrictions unfamiliar to users of open DeFi protocols. The commercial question is whether those features make institutional Bitcoin exposure more usable without creating too many layers of counterparty risk and operational cost.

What to watch next

Useful measures will include verified reserves over time, the number of eligible trading participants, actual volumes, the speed of deposits and redemptions, and any institutional collateral use. Readers should avoid treating a new token listing as an increase in Bitcoin's supply. The underlying BTC remains the backing asset; CBTC creates an additional instrument through which that economic exposure can circulate, with its own terms and risks.

Primary source: EDX Markets and BitSafe company release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s report on restrictions affecting another Bitcoin-backed token.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Ripple Highlights Custody Services as 37 Banks Prepare Euro Stablecoin
summary: Ripple highlighted custody, governance, and banking integration as institutions prepare for Qivalis’ planned euro stablecoin. Its assessment connected those requirements to its existing services, citing clients BBVA and DZ BANK within the 37-bank consortium. Ripple Outlines Custody and Governance Re...
content:
Ripple highlighted custody, governance, and banking integration as institutions prepare for Qivalis’ planned euro stablecoin. Its assessment connected those requirements to its existing services, citing clients BBVA and DZ BANK within the 37-bank consortium.

Key Takeaways

  • BBVA and DZ BANK already use Ripple Custody for digital assets.
  • Each bank faces its own decision on safeguarding customer holdings.
  • Qivalis’ issuance plans remain subject to regulatory requirements.

Ripple Outlines Custody and Governance Requirements

Ripple highlighted its custody services on Nov. 9 as it examined bank custody requirements for Qivalis’ planned euro stablecoin. The company cited existing clients, including BBVA and DZ BANK, and described how banks would need to safeguard client holdings, enforce operational controls, and connect digital assets with existing systems. It placed those functions within its broader services spanning issuance, custody, governance, settlement, and redemption.

Cassie Craddock, Ripple’s vice president and managing director, stated:

“Now that the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation (MiCA) is established across Europe, the region’s banks are emboldened to launch the digital asset offerings that their customers are asking for.”

Individual banks could retain custody or delegate it to another provider, Ripple explained. Its technology connects with banking software through application programming interfaces, which let systems exchange data and instructions. Software-defined policies, or rules enforced by software, govern access, approvals, separation of duties, and jurisdictional controls.

BBVA and DZ BANK Illustrate Different Custody Uses

BBVA’s custody agreement with Ripple supported bitcoin and ether services for retail customers in Spain. Ripple said the bank retained control of its cryptographic keys and responsibility for protecting client assets. The relationship also extends to custody operations in Switzerland and Turkey.

DZ BANK, a German cooperative banking group’s central institution, selected Metaco’s custody platform for institutional digital asset services. Metaco is a Swiss custody technology provider acquired by Ripple in 2023. The German bank sought to handle crypto securities under the country’s Electronic Securities Act within established capital-market processes.

The Nov. 9 assessment described integration with DZ BANK’s existing asset-management and custody operations. One early application involved a Siemens tokenized bond held by DZ BANK and Union Investment, a German asset manager. The examples covered retail crypto holdings and institutional securities, illustrating different uses for Ripple’s technology.

Qivalis Prepares Issuance Following Dutch Authorization

Qivalis, an Amsterdam-based joint venture, expanded to 37 member banks across 15 countries after adding 25 institutions in May. Participants include ING, BNP Paribas, BBVA, and DZ BANK. Its planned token would support payments, settlement, and tokenized assets, which digitally represent assets recorded on a blockchain.

De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), the Dutch central bank, granted Qivalis authorization as an electronic money institution. Its register of authorized activities lists issuance, distribution, and redemption permissions effective Oct. 13. The license places Qivalis under ongoing DNB supervision.

The venture plans a full-reserve stablecoin model, with each token backed 1:1 by reserves. Qivalis would handle issuance and redemption under its own authorizations and technology. Individual institutions would determine their customer custody arrangements, including whether to retain custody or use another provider.

In its Oct. 14 announcement, Qivalis outlined planned issuance within the following months, subject to applicable Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation requirements and publication of its white paper. Distribution would run through eligible banks, exchanges, payment providers, and financial market infrastructure participants.

title: 21X and LayerZero Report 10,000 Onchain Order Matches Per Second in Pilot
summary: European trading venue 21X and LayerZero say a private, permissioned deployment of Zero handled 10,000 order matches per second in a month-long technical pilot. The companies disclosed the result on November 4, reporting a 45-fold performance…
content:
TL;DR: European trading venue 21X and LayerZero say a private, permissioned deployment of Zero handled 10,000 order matches per second in a month-long technical pilot. The companies disclosed the result on November 4, reporting a 45-fold performance improvement against the EVM layer-two baseline they used.

European trading venue 21X and LayerZero say a private, permissioned deployment of Zero handled 10,000 order matches per second in a month-long technical pilot. The companies disclosed the result on November 4, reporting a 45-fold performance improvement against the EVM layer-two baseline they used. It is an unusually specific benchmark in a market full of throughput promises, although an internal pilot is not the same as sustained production trading under real market stress.

The scope of the test

The partners say they ran a fully onchain central limit order book with an emphasis on US equity tokens. Matching orders onchain is technically different from recording a trade after an offchain matching engine has already decided the outcome. The reported throughput would therefore address a genuine challenge for blockchain-based venues. The private instance also matters: network membership and visibility can be controlled differently from a permissionless public chain. Comparing the result with public networks requires care because validators, transaction patterns, hardware assumptions and network conditions may not be equivalent.

Why institutions want control

Regulated markets need surveillance, market-access controls, records, resilience and procedures for trade errors. Some institutions are unwilling or unable to expose all transactional details on a public ledger. A permissioned environment can allow more predictable operations while still using programmable execution and a shared data layer. The trade-off is that permissioning changes trust and governance: someone must define who can participate, how upgrades occur and what happens when the network is unavailable. A fast benchmark does not settle those governance questions or prove that the system is suitable for every regulated market.

The meaning of the 45x figure

Performance comparisons are only as good as their baseline. LayerZero says the pilot was around 45 times faster than a referenced layer-two EVM setup. That is useful for the experiment's stated conditions, but it should not be generalized to all blockchains or all workloads. Throughput can vary when orders are cancelled, modified or subjected to complex compliance checks. Latency, finality, settlement integrity and recovery from outages matter as well. A trading venue would also need to demonstrate that market data and order priority remain fair at high volumes.

Where tokenization meets exchange engineering

Tokenized securities are often described primarily as a custody or issuance problem. But active exchange trading introduces difficult requirements around price-time priority, matching, market making and operations during volatile conditions. The partnership suggests infrastructure providers are taking those less visible tasks seriously. The promise of running an order book onchain is more auditable shared state, but that benefit depends on execution design and on who can inspect the records. A private test is a starting point rather than proof of an operating securities market.

What should come after a pilot

The next milestones are independent testing, disclosure of methodology, resilient deployment across multiple participants and approval for any relevant regulated activities. Real trading volume and incident history would be more persuasive than repeating peak performance figures. If 21X and LayerZero can demonstrate those outcomes, this could become an important example of high-throughput financial infrastructure. Until then, the strongest conclusion is that the companies reported a promising benchmark under controlled conditions.

Primary source: 21X and LayerZero Labs joint release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s report on the wider push toward tokenized securities venues.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: IRS Is Sending Crypto Users Tax Letters—Here’s What You Need to Know
summary: Clinton Donnelly, CEO of Cryptotaxaudit, warned that, based on the volume the company is seeing, the IRS is using a letter campaign to pressure crypto taxpayers to review their past filings. However, he explained that receiving one letter does not imply wrongdoing. Cryptotaxaudit CEO Alerts of Massi...
content:
1. News
  2. Crypto News
  3. IRS Is Sending Crypto Users Tax Letters—Here's What You Need to Know

Published:Nov 9, 2026, 8:40 PM EST

Clinton Donnelly, CEO of Cryptotaxaudit, warned that, based on the volume the company is seeing, the IRS is using a letter campaign to pressure crypto taxpayers to review their past filings. However, he explained that receiving one letter does not imply wrongdoing.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 9, 2026, 8:40 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • The IRS is sending a massive wave of Letter 6174 notices to pressure crypto users on tax compliance.
  • The notices alert taxpayers that the IRS knows of their crypto activity and seeks accurate returns.
  • Experts advise against rushing to amend filings, as the letters are reminders, not proof of guilt.

Cryptotaxaudit CEO Alerts of Massive IRS Campaign Against Crypto Taxpayers

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is targeting cryptocurrency taxpayers in a massive push, and crypto tax executives are alarmed by the ongoing campaign’s size.

Clinton Donnelly, CEO of Cryptotaxaudit, a company that offers crypto tax returns, crypto gain calculations, and forensic crypto analysis services, reported a growing crypto taxpayer-focused campaign using Letter 6174 notices.

On social media, Donnelly described the surge as “alarming,” revealing that dozens of people, including the firm’s own clients, have contacted the company after receiving notices.

“This is no longer an isolated handful of cases,” he stressed. Donnelly explained that Letter 6174 notices were voluntary compliance letters, meaning that the IRS has information about your crypto activity and wants you to review whether you have met your tax reporting duties.

Before, Donnelly detected a rise in these letters in the past six weeks, calling it “a vague scare.”

“They send these letters out at roughly the rate of 10,000 a month, and they send them to people that they know have had cryptocurrency transactions. And it’s simply educational. That’s how the IRS looks at it. It’s an educational letter,” he assessed at that time.

But now, he acknowledges that the IRS might be pressuring crypto payers, as it has before, to review past filings and take corrective action. Still, he clarified that receiving one of these letters was not indicative of wrongdoing.

“Threw It Right in the Trash”

First sent to taxpayers in 2019, Letter 6174 notices state that the IRS has “information that you have or had one or more accounts containing virtual currency but may not know the requirements for reporting transactions involving virtual currency, which include cryptocurrency and non-crypto virtual currencies.”

At the same time, the letter calls for filing amended returns or delinquent returns after failing to file them for one or more taxable years, without pointing to specific inconsistencies.

“DO NOT rush into amending tax returns or sending information to the IRS without understanding your position first. Letters 6174 and 6174-A generally do not require a direct response, but you should review the instructions carefully,” Donnelly concluded.

Multiple respondents on X said they had recently received one of the letters. Joel Schwartz, CTO Emeritus and member of Ripple’s Board of Directors, said he got one in the mail a few days ago, but disregarded it.

“Threw it right in the trash,” Schwartz posted. “It’s basically just a reminder to follow the law.”

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Schroders Emerging-Market Bond Strategy Moves Onto Solana Through Centrifuge
summary: Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge…
content:
TL;DR: Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure.

Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure. It is notable because the assets are not a cryptocurrency basket: investors are being offered a blockchain-native route to a conventional, actively managed fixed-income strategy with its own risks and investment processes.

What the partners announced

Centrifuge says the initiative will introduce tokenized exposure to the Schroders emerging-market bond fund. Schroders manages more than $1 trillion in assets across its business, according to the announcement, and has decades of experience investing in debt issued by emerging-market governments and companies. That corporate scale provides context for the partnership; it is not an estimate of how much capital has entered this particular onchain fund. The launch represents Schroders' first Solana deployment, a specific milestone that should not be confused with a wholesale shift of the manager's portfolios to public blockchains.

What investors are actually exposed to

Emerging-market bonds can offer access to currencies, credit risks and interest-rate conditions very different from those facing US Treasury bills. The underlying portfolio may be affected by sovereign finances, corporate defaults, currency movements and changes in global borrowing costs. Tokenization does not eliminate those exposures. It changes how interests in an investment strategy can be issued, recorded, distributed or serviced. Investors need to understand the fund's legal structure, eligibility, fees, dealing arrangements and the precise way token holdings map to recognized ownership. Those details ultimately determine whether the product meets their requirements.

Why Solana and Centrifuge are relevant

Solana's appeal to financial product developers includes its transaction throughput and low per-transaction fees, while Centrifuge focuses on the specialist infrastructure needed to operate tokenized funds. The challenge is making asset management routines work with a public network without losing compliance controls. Fund subscriptions, redemptions, transfer restrictions and investor records must align with the legally constituted vehicle. A fast chain is helpful, but it cannot replace the fund administrator, custodian or manager. Operational success depends on the quality of those connections, not simply on the number of transactions the blockchain can process.

A bridge between two kinds of finance

Much of the early RWA market concentrated on tokenized cash and short-dated US government debt. An actively managed emerging-market bond strategy is a different proposition because valuation, liquidity and portfolio turnover can be more complicated. A market may be open at all hours even when underlying bonds trade within narrower windows. That difference makes pricing and redemption policies essential. The value proposition could be broader distribution and improved processing, but investors should not infer that every share can be redeemed instantly or that tokenization creates round-the-clock liquidity in the underlying securities.

What would demonstrate real adoption

The next useful evidence would include an initial live issuance, assets held in the tokenized structure, participating distributors, supported jurisdictions and how subscriptions and redemptions actually settle. Over time, the question is whether blockchain infrastructure improves operational efficiency and attracts new investors without weakening fund protections. The announcement is a meaningful institutional experiment, but the practical success of the fund will rest on ordinary asset-management disciplines as much as on Solana technology.

Primary source: Centrifuge official product announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s report on Solana’s infrastructure and institutional RWA growth.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: HIVE, MARA mine more Bitcoin but earn less as crypto prices fall
summary: Both miners reported higher Bitcoin production but lower mining revenue and rising electricity costs as they expanded their AI infrastructure businesses.
content:
HIVE Digital Technologies and MARA Holdings mined more Bitcoin in the September quarter than a year earlier but reported lower mining revenue, as weaker Bitcoin prices outweighed gains in production.

According to their latest regulatory filings, HIVE’s Bitcoin production increased 49% to 1,070 Bitcoin (BTC), while mining revenue fell 7.4% to $76 million. MARA reported a similar pattern, with production rising 5% to 2,247 BTC and Bitcoin mining revenue dropping 34% to $159 million.

Both companies reported higher power bills and equipment charges. HIVE’s electricity costs rose 20% to $45.6 million, while MARA’s purchased energy costs increased 12% to $48.1 million as it expanded its owned mining operations.

HIVE also recorded a $31.2 million noncash write-down on mining equipment, citing “depressed mining economics,” while MARA separately wrote off $12 million involving mining rigs and equipment under restructuring plans.  

Both results add to signs of pressure on Bitcoin mining economics. American Bitcoin last week reported weaker mining margins despite a treasury-driven quarterly profit, while Core Scientific said it plans to leave mining entirely by year-end.

HIVE and MARA expand AI businesses alongside mining

Unlike Core Scientific, HIVE and MARA are both continuing to invest in Bitcoin mining alongside artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

HIVE’s HPC hosting revenue rose 71% to $8.8 million in the September quarter, accounting for 10.4% of total revenue. The company has described its strategy as combining cash flow from mining with recurring revenue from AI infrastructure.

Related: American Bitcoin’s $126M profit masks mining pressure as rivals turn to AI

HIVE said it anticipates spending up to $493 million over 36 months to expand its HPC operations, including acquiring land, building out data center infrastructure and buying up GPUs. The company reported spending $145.3 million toward that expansion as of the filing.

HIVE also plans to spend about $35 million converting its Toronto facility into a Tier-III data center. Meanwhile, it continues to expand its mining infrastructure, targeting a 100-megawatt substation expansion at its Yguazú site in Paraguay during 2026.

MARA is also developing AI infrastructure through its Exaion subsidiary and a partnership with Starwood Digital Ventures. It said it intends to operate sites that can shift between workloads depending on economics, demand and grid conditions, with Bitcoin mining remaining the foundation of its platform.

Treasury gains lift MARA profit, HIVE reports quarterly loss

HIVE’s Nasdaq-listed shares fell 1.7% to $1.78 in after-hours trading Monday, according to Google Finance, after closing the regular session up 1.7% at $1.81.

The company reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $84.9 million, down 2.7% from a year earlier but above the $79.4 million consensus estimate listed by MarketBeat. 

Meanwhile, MARA reported net income attributable to common stockholders of $634.4 million, up from $123.1 million a year earlier, and included substantial fair-value gains on digital assets and digital asset receivables.

MARA reported quarterly revenue of $164.2 million, down 35% year-on-year, and diluted earnings of $1.28 a share, up from 27 cents, while its shares were little changed at $6.64 in after-hours trading Monday after closing up 4.6%.

title: Ethereum Foundation and Vitalik Buterin Sued Over Employee Firing After ‘Suicide Pledge’
summary: Former Ethereum Foundation employee Kayleen Fulton has filed a federal lawsuit alleging wrongful termination, disability discrimination, and medical leave violations—and said she was dismissed after organizing pushback to a document that included a “suicide pledge.” Timeline of Termination The Ether...
content:
Former Ethereum Foundation employee Kayleen Fulton has filed a federal lawsuit alleging wrongful termination, disability discrimination, and medical leave violations—and said she was dismissed after organizing pushback to a document that included a “suicide pledge.”

Key Takeaways

  • Kayleen Fulton sued the Ethereum Foundation after her April 6 firing following a cancer disclosure.
  • The case exposes governance friction after 53 Ethereum Foundation staff protested a mandatory “suicide pledge.”
  • Fulton pursues 11 legal claims in federal court while an NLRB unfair labor practice charge stays pending.

Timeline of Termination

The Ethereum Foundation and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin are facing a federal lawsuit filed by a former employee who alleges she was wrongfully terminated after disclosing an ovarian cancer diagnosis, and organizing staff opposition to a controversial organizational mandate.

According to a complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, Kayleen Fulton, who previously led the Ethereum Foundation’s Protocol Support team, was dismissed on April 6—just 13 days after informing senior management of her diagnosis.

The lawsuit names six defendants: the Ethereum Foundation’s Swiss entity, Stiftung Ethereum; its Singapore affiliate, Ethereum Asia Pacific Ltd.; executive Bastian Aue; Buterin; and two human resources service providers, Lightsource HR Global LLC and Vensure Employer Services Inc.

Fulton alleges disability discrimination, retaliation, interference with medical leave rights, and wrongful termination under federal and Colorado law. She is seeking lost wages, compensatory and punitive damages, legal fees, and invalidation of her separation agreement.

At the center of the dispute is an organizational document known as the Mandate, which the Ethereum Foundation’s board distributed to employees Feb. 25. According to the complaint, the document contained a provision called the “Source Seppuku License,” which included a pledge that contributors would take their own lives with a sword if they failed to uphold its terms.

The provision sparked widespread opposition among employees, with 79 staff members voting to remove it. Buterin, a member of the foundation’s board, subsequently told employees that significant changes were being considered in response to their concerns.

However, the final version, published March 13, retained the disputed language in a stylized illustration featuring cartoon characters. The foundation also recorded the document on the Ethereum blockchain, according to the lawsuit.

Staff Protest and Alleged Retaliation

Fulton and another employee, Trent Van Epps, organized a protest letter signed by 53 foundation employees opposing a requirement to personally endorse the Mandate or face termination. Although management ultimately allowed dissenting employees to retain their jobs, Fulton and Van Epps were fired April 6. Their complaint alleges they were selectively targeted for organizing the protest.

She alleges the foundation dismissed her less than two weeks after she disclosed her cancer diagnosis, despite a strong performance record and no prior disciplinary action. The complaint claims management failed to address her request for employment protection or medical leave before terminating her without a specific explanation. Facing the imminent loss of health insurance, Fulton signed a separation agreement waiving legal claims, but she is now challenging its enforceability, including a provision requiring arbitration in Singapore.

The lawsuit cites a recorded conversation in which Buterin allegedly questioned whether rewarding employees for challenging management would encourage further dissent. Her attorneys argue the remarks support claims of retaliatory dismissal, although the complaint does not establish that Buterin personally ordered her termination.

The complaint brings 11 claims, including disability discrimination, medical leave violations and intentional infliction of emotional distress. Although Fulton seeks back pay and damages, the filing does not specify a total dollar amount.

According to the complaint, Fulton filed a discrimination charge with the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission on June 2 and received a notice of right to sue Sept. 23. She also filed a separate unfair labor practice charge with the National Labor Relations Board, which remained pending when the lawsuit was filed.

title: Ondo Claims $4B in Tokenized Assets as RWA Market Gains Institutional Depth
summary: Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data. They…
content:
TL;DR: Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data.

Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data. They illustrate how tokenized finance is broadening beyond a small set of Treasury products, but the definitions behind a ranking matter as much as the impressive headline figure.

What Ondo is counting

The corrected release says Ondo ranks first among 203 platforms tracked by RWA.xyz by the market capitalization of tokenized products and accounts for roughly a tenth of non-stablecoin RWA value. The comparison excludes stablecoins and uses the data provider's classification of assets and platforms. Readers should not confuse it with Ondo's revenue, cash on its balance sheet, net inflows in a single day or the trading volume of the ONDO token. Tokenized product value can also move with prices and redemptions, so the number should be treated as a dated snapshot rather than an immutable milestone.

Why the asset mix matters

The category now spans short-term government debt, funds, equities and other exposures offered through various legal and custody structures. Those instruments may all be called real-world assets while providing very different rights, liquidity and redemption procedures. A tokenized money market interest can behave unlike a tokenized stock, and neither should be analyzed simply as an unsecured crypto token. The key question is what claim the holder owns, who maintains the legal records and how a user receives the underlying value when a transaction or redemption is requested.

Distribution may be as important as issuance

Issuing a blockchain representation is relatively straightforward compared with making it useful to investors and institutions. Platforms need identity checks, compliant distribution, secondary transfer controls, custody arrangements and ongoing servicing. The scale reported by Ondo suggests that these practical layers have become commercially significant. Yet a large holder count does not disclose how assets are concentrated, whether addresses represent individuals or intermediaries, or what proportion trades regularly. A platform can be large by outstanding value while some products remain relatively illiquid.

Corrected releases deserve careful reading

Ondo issued this information as a correction, making it particularly important to use the complete revised text rather than an earlier headline copied across aggregators. Rankings also depend on the measurement date and definitions used by the data provider. A later expansion of coverage or reclassification could change relative positions without any shift in underlying user demand. Readers should therefore seek source methodology and product-level information before interpreting a top ranking as evidence of an uncontested or permanent market lead.

The next test for RWAs

The strongest sign of maturation will be whether tokenized products are used in ordinary financial workflows: collateral management, settlement, portfolio allocation and redemptions. Transparent asset backing, enforceable rights and resilient operations will matter more than product count alone. Ondo's milestone is a useful indicator of scale, provided it is presented as a company-reported snapshot of tokenized assets rather than a promise about future returns or market dominance.

Primary source: Ondo Finance corrected company release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s coverage of the infrastructure forming around tokenized securities.

title: Ether Treasury Sharplink’s Q3 Profit Soars 620%—but There’s a Catch
summary: Sharplink reported a Q3 net income of $751.4 million, a more than sevenfold year-over-year increase, driven primarily by unrealized gains on its cryptocurrency holdings. Modest Revenue Growth and Cost Controls Nasdaq-listed ether treasury company Sharplink reported a more than sevenfold increase in ...
content:
Sharplink reported a Q3 net income of $751.4 million, a more than sevenfold year-over-year increase, driven primarily by unrealized gains on its cryptocurrency holdings.

Key Takeaways

  • Sharplink reported Q3 net income of $751.4M on Nov. 9, up sevenfold year-over-year.
  • Staking on Ethereum surged 27% to $13.1M, signaling institutional shift toward yield-generating crypto assets.
  • Sharplink plans to deploy capital from its $125M Galaxy fund into onchain yield opportunities.

Modest Revenue Growth and Cost Controls

Nasdaq-listed ether treasury company Sharplink reported a more than sevenfold increase in third-quarter net income to $751.4 million. However, nearly most of the profit stemmed from unrealized gains on its cryptocurrency holdings rather than cash-generating operations.

According to financial results released Nov. 9, Sharplink recorded net income of $751.4 million for the three months ended Sept. 30. That compares with net income of $104.3 million, or 62 cents per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. The results show that Sharplink recorded $676.7 million in unrealized gains, representing approximately 90% of its reported net income. The company also recognized $75.2 million in net realized gains, primarily associated with Ethereum treasury activities, including liquid staking.

Beyond gains on its cryptocurrency holdings, Sharplink reported more modest revenue growth. Total revenue increased 24% year-over-year to $13.5 million, up from $10.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. Staking revenue, which accounted for roughly 97% of total revenue, climbed 27% to $13.1 million from $10.3 million.

The growth reflected the company’s efforts to generate income from its Ethereum treasury rather than relying strictly on asset appreciation.

Sharplink also reported an 8% decline in selling, general, and administrative expenses to $11 million, down from $12 million a year earlier, reflecting improved cost management during its institutional expansion. Cash and cash equivalents rose to $47.9 million as of Sept. 30, up from $28.5 million at the end of December 2025.

Sharplink CEO Joseph Chalom attributed the results to execution of the company’s treasury strategy.

“Our strong third-quarter performance reflects our progress in executing our Ethereum treasury strategy and further strengthening our institutional-grade treasury platform,” Chalom said in a statement.

Treasury Expansion and Staking Strategy

During the quarter, Sharplink continued expanding its cryptocurrency reserve, holding approximately 892,708 ether (ETH) as of Sept. 30. By Nov. 2, holdings had increased to roughly 895,117 ETH. The company valued its digital assets at approximately $2.1 billion at the end of September under U.S. GAAP.

As part of its yield strategy, Sharplink completed a $200 million ETH staking allocation through decentralized protocol Lido on Sept. 28. The transaction provided wrapped staked ETH (wstETH), enabling participation in staking rewards while maintaining exposure to decentralized finance opportunities.

The company also advanced its partnership with Galaxy Digital through the Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund, launched in August with $125 million in initial commitments. Sharplink contributed $100 million and Galaxy Digital committed $25 million. The fund began deploying capital into onchain opportunities during the third quarter.

Additionally, Sharplink made a strategic equity investment in Blockspace, an Ethereum infrastructure company specializing in validation and staking services. Chalom said the initiatives align with the company’s goal to treat digital assets as yield-generating capital.

“These milestones reflect our belief that ETH should be managed as a productive operating asset rather than simply held for potential appreciation,” Chalom said.

Sharplink Chairman and Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin expressed confidence in long-term growth, pointing to institutional adoption of Ethereum and expanding blockchain-based financial infrastructure, including JPMorgan’s deposit token initiatives and asset tokenization.

Shares in Sharplink (SBET) finished the day down 1.76% at a price of $6.13, pushing the firm’s monthly loss to nearly 29%. Over the last year, SBET has fallen almost 49%.

title: Dinari Adds Broadridge Voting Rails to Tokenized US Shares
summary: Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of…
content:
TL;DR: Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure.

Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure. The development highlights shareholder governance as a core feature of credible tokenization, not an optional extra on a trading app.

What the integration provides

According to the companies, eligible dShare holders can exercise voting rights associated with the underlying US equities through Broadridge's proxy systems. Those votes are intended to enter the same formal processes used by traditional shareholders. This is more concrete than giving token holders a separate community poll about a company. Shareholder resolutions, board elections and other corporate actions depend on recognized ownership records, deadlines and entitlement calculations. The release describes an integration of these processes, although it does not publish a full end-to-end test record for each supported company.

Tokenization can change the wrapper, not the rights

A user buying exposure to a company's share may assume the resulting token comes with the same rights as a share in a conventional brokerage account. That assumption is dangerous unless the product's legal structure supports it. Some tokens are claims on intermediaries, while others are issued and serviced in ways designed to preserve shareholder entitlements. Dinari's integration addresses part of that problem by moving voting instructions through established channels. Investors should still verify which tokens qualify, whether voting is available in their jurisdiction and how any intermediary custody arrangements affect their position.

Why Broadridge is a natural participant

Broadridge already handles a large volume of investor communications and governance workflows in traditional markets. Connecting these systems to a tokenized product can be more practical than reconstructing every corporate-action process from scratch. That matters because an issuer cannot simply ignore events such as stock splits, tender offers or changes in the shareholder register. There may also be timing conflicts between token transfer windows and voting record dates. The harder task is keeping balances, entitlements and instruction chains aligned as holders move between wallets and supported intermediaries.

Access and ownership remain distinct

An improved voting experience does not automatically make a tokenized share freely transferable, exchange-listed or protected identically in every jurisdiction. Eligibility, investor verification and local securities rules may still apply. Likewise, a voting feature says little about trading liquidity or the robustness of the underlying custody model. Broadridge and Dinari's announcement is best understood as one part of the market's operational maturation. It makes a necessary ownership function more visible, but cannot settle every legal or commercial question around tokenized equities.

What to watch next

Useful evidence would include the number of supported issuers, actual voting participation by eligible holders, records of successful proxy delivery and support for other corporate actions. For asset managers and platforms considering tokenized stock distribution, governance infrastructure is a test of whether the product behaves like an investment or merely tracks its price. That distinction will become more important as institutions offer these instruments to a broader audience.

Primary source: Broadridge and Dinari joint release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s coverage of transfer-agent participation in tokenized stock infrastructure.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Elliptic said North Korean hackers used memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, EU authorities asked the finance industry to develop common standards for tokenized securities, and Zcash developers proposed cutting block times from 25 to 20 seconds.

North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic

North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch.

The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain.

Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities

The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities.

Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers.

The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets.

The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards.

In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money. 

Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade

Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade. 

On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on GitHub, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade.

The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps.

The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently.

The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.

The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap.

title: Broadridge Says Blockchain Repo Platform Processed $7.6T in October
summary: Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest…
content:
TL;DR: Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens.

Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens. It also needs context: a month of cumulative repo activity is a flow measure, not $7.6 trillion of newly created blockchain assets.

What the volume measures

Repurchase agreements are short-term financing arrangements in which securities are sold with an agreement to repurchase them, often against cash collateral. They are a major part of the funding market for banks and dealers. Broadridge's figure represents cumulative transaction processing through its DLR system during October, while the average daily figure gives a sense of ongoing throughput. It should not be mistaken for assets permanently locked in a protocol or a standalone market capitalization. Repeated financing transactions can generate large summed volume even while the underlying collateral turns over.

Why institutions use distributed ledgers here

Repo involves collateral records, cash movement, timing, reconciliations and multiple operational teams. A shared transaction environment can reduce disagreements about the state of a deal and help participants coordinate settlement. That is an attractive use case for distributed infrastructure precisely because the counterparties may already be regulated financial institutions that need detailed permissions and controls. Broadridge's announcement presents DLR as a production platform, rather than a proof of concept. Still, the release does not by itself quantify net cost savings for individual users or independently verify every reported operational benefit.

The next platform is broader than repo

Broadridge is using the DLR experience to promote its DLX platform, which it says supports issuance, trading, settlement, financing and asset servicing. This is a commercial strategy to connect workflows that are currently separate. A tokenized asset is more useful if it can be financed, transferred, serviced and reported without expensive custom integrations. The difficulty is coordination with existing custody, legal rights and market infrastructure. Moving one record onchain does not magically resolve differences between firms' processes, and institutional adoption may continue to favor permissioned arrangements.

A scale signal with practical caveats

The October number suggests substantial existing demand for shared-ledger settlement in securities financing. It does not mean all traditional repo has moved onto a blockchain, nor does it imply that users can trade the underlying collateral publicly. Differences between tokenized records, ownership registers and conventional settlement obligations can be legally significant. Readers should look for comparable periods, the number and diversity of participating institutions, operational resilience and the share of transactions that run without manual intervention. Those indicators help distinguish a very large gross number from lasting efficiency gains.

Where the story goes next

Broadridge expects tokenized finance to extend further through normal market operations in 2027. The most revealing milestones will be independent institutional adoption and recurring transaction volume across multiple product types. For crypto investors, the lesson is to separate blockchain use as infrastructure from token speculation. A huge processing volume can demonstrate a serious enterprise application without creating direct demand for a liquid crypto token.

Primary source: Broadridge Financial Solutions company release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s reporting on Europe’s settlement modernization plans.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: North Korea’s $6.3B Binance Hack Takes a Strange Turn With Meme Coins
summary: North Korean launderers have turned to disposable meme coins to disguise proceeds from Binance’s roughly $6.3 billion hack. Elliptic identified related tactics on three blockchains, adding cheap, repeatable obstacles to efforts to trace the stolen assets. Meme Coins Complicate the Binance Hack Trail...
content:
North Korean launderers have turned to disposable meme coins to disguise proceeds from Binance’s roughly $6.3 billion hack. Elliptic identified related tactics on three blockchains, adding cheap, repeatable obstacles to efforts to trace the stolen assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Linked wallets controlled nearly all trading in the disposable tokens.
  • Launderers recycled sale proceeds to finance new token launches.
  • Stolen assets converted into bitcoin reached about $225 million.

Meme Coins Complicate the Binance Hack Trail

North Korean launderers used meme coins and obscure tokens on Tron, Solana, and Near, Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Tom Robinson explained on Nov. 9. Tron and Near involved newly created coins; Solana relied on existing assets.

Robinson wrote:

“Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype. North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them, creating tokens that nobody else wants to buy and using them to disguise the movement of stolen funds.”

On Near, one group bought the new coins with stolen cryptocurrency through token liquidity pools. Other wallets sold into the same pools and collected nearly matching proceeds, separating the sending and receiving addresses.

Six tokens created between Nov. 5 and Nov. 7 handled about 117,000 NEAR ($430,000), with almost no outside trading. Each launch cost about $90. Five creators received funding from earlier token sales shortly before launching replacements.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed last month’s Binance theft to North Korea on Oct. 31, identifying the operation as Tradertraitor, a state-sponsored North Korean group targeting cryptocurrency businesses.

However, North Korea denied responsibility for the hack on Nov. 3. Kim Yo-jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, called the FBI’s accusations a “grave political provocation” intended to damage the country’s reputation.

Binance Theft Triggered a Race Against Freezes

Stolen assets from the Oct. 29 Binance attack mixed with proceeds from September’s Bitget theft, Chainalysis found. The firm cited this overlap in attributing the Binance theft to Tradertraitor. Its assessment drew on blockchain activity observed in the hours after the attack.

The attacker attempted to evade freezes through rapid stablecoin conversions, exchanging $325 million in funds for approximately $285 million in ether over nearly 20 minutes. Ether lacks the issuer-controlled freezes available for those stablecoins.

Elliptic flagged a worthless Tron token created solely for laundering on Nov. 2, and stolen solana moved through thinly traded tokens the next day. Elliptic previously traced at least $24 million through a similar scheme after the 2025 Bybit theft.

Explaining the layered approach, Robinson stated:

“North Korea’s launderers rarely rely on a single technique. Instead, they layer many cheap techniques, each adding a little more delay. Homemade meme tokens are simply one more layer.”

Thousands of Wallets Lead Into Bitcoin

By Nov. 2, stolen assets had passed through approximately 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains. Fixed timing and blind retries of failed operations without adjustment indicated conventional automation. Elliptic found no evidence of AI-directed decisions.

A Nov. 7 update counted more than 20,000 wallets, 16 blockchains, and at least 65,000 transactions. Elliptic tracked conversions into approximately 2,300 bitcoin, worth $175 million then, from assets including solana, XRP, and tron.

Converted proceeds reached about 3,000 bitcoin, worth $225 million by Nov. 9. Elliptic also traced roughly 7,000 ether (about $15 million worth) into Tornado Cash, a mixer allowing pooled deposits to be withdrawn to different addresses. The firm estimated that only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out.

On exposure through trading pools, the Elliptic chief scientist warned:

“A wallet that received its funds from a liquidity pool should not be treated as clean by default, as it may sit just two swaps away from stolen funds.”

title: Wall Street Calls AI Sell-Off Overdone as Earnings Put the Rebound to the Test
summary: Morgan Stanley and UBS argue investors have become too pessimistic about AI. CoreWeave’s earnings and the political backlash will test whether the optimism is justified.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: CRWV NVDA

Morgan Stanley and UBS argue investors have become too pessimistic about AI. CoreWeave’s earnings and the political backlash will test whether the optimism is justified.

Wall Street’s AI sell-off has produced a familiar confrontation: investors worried that an extraordinary spending boom is running into political and financial limits, and major brokerages arguing the market has become too pessimistic.

Morgan Stanley and UBS called last week’s rout overdone, Reuters reported on November 9. Their argument is that tougher scrutiny of data centres need not derail demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The next earnings releases will test whether that distinction holds up.

For investors, the disagreement is consequential. A slower construction schedule could reduce immediate spending pressure. It could also delay revenue while borrowing costs keep accumulating. The same delay can look manageable from a long-term demand forecast and painful from a company’s cash-flow statement.

Why Wall Street says the AI sell-off went too far

Morgan Stanley’s interpretation, according to Reuters, is that some projects could move from 2028 into 2029 rather than disappear. Its analysts argued that a longer investment cycle could ease supply-demand imbalances and improve the credit outlook.

The bank recommended “buying the drop.” HSBC also said it was increasing equity exposure following the correction, while UBS argued investors had become too negative on political risk, credit risk and AI spending.

That is a case for reassessing expectations, rather than evidence that every company caught in the decline is inexpensive. Demand for computing, the price paid for a stock and the cost of financing a data centre are separate questions.

The argument also puts more weight on delivery. Investors will need companies to turn spending commitments into usable capacity, customer payments and a credible path through their financing obligations.

The political backlash is real

There is a substantive policy dispute behind the market anxiety. Reuters reported on November 6 that Democrats plan legislation addressing data-centre electricity costs, independent testing of advanced AI systems and corporate liability when products cause harm.

Senator Chuck Schumer identified protection from higher energy bills as a priority. Representative Lori Trahan’s plans include independent evaluations of leading models and clearer liability rules, according to the report.

President Donald Trump’s opposition creates a significant obstacle to passing restrictions. Yet dismissing the entire political risk would also go too far. Committee control can increase pressure through hearings and demands for information, even when legislation stalls.

“The probability of legislation is much higher than people anticipate,” Raymond James policy researcher Ed Mills told Reuters.

The distinction for shareholders is between a campaign promise, a proposed bill and a binding rule. They have different implications for project schedules and costs. A market repricing based on the most restrictive possible outcome may overstate the danger; one that assumes no change may understate it.

CoreWeave provides a near-term test

CoreWeave has scheduled its third-quarter earnings call for November 10 at 5 p.m. US Eastern. The AI cloud provider offers a more immediate test of infrastructure economics than a distant estimate of total AI demand.

Its second-quarter results show both sides of the debate. Revenue rose to $2.575 billion from $1.212 billion a year earlier, while adjusted net loss widened to $567 million from $130 million. Adjusted net loss is a non-GAAP measure.

Chart: Brave New Coin, using CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 release. Adjusted net loss is a non-GAAP measure; loss bars show magnitude.

CoreWeave also reported approximately $104 billion of revenue backlog at June 30. The company says that measure includes committed customer contracts whose recognition depends on delivery and service availability. A large backlog therefore offers visibility into potential revenue, without being cash already collected.

Investors will be looking for the pace at which that demand becomes revenue, the cost of bringing capacity online and the terms on which expansion is financed. Strong growth can coexist with substantial losses; an earnings beat does not automatically settle the funding question.

Power and financing can change the story

The infrastructure boom is also becoming a power-supply story. BNC’s coverage of Anthropic’s energy commitments and IPO valuation pressures illustrates how electricity access and the price investors will pay for AI growth are increasingly connected.

Companies can have willing customers and still encounter limits on available power, equipment or construction. Each obstacle matters because expensive infrastructure must be funded before it produces its full return.

Investors should also distinguish a delay that allows suppliers to catch up from one caused by customers withdrawing demand. The first may spread spending over a longer period; the second can undermine the revenue assumptions used to justify the investment. Management explanations, changes in delivery schedules and the terms of new contracts will matter more than treating every postponement as either healthy or disastrous.

The interest-rate backdrop offers limited comfort. The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75%–4% in October, but two policymakers preferred an increase. That leaves financing conditions as a live part of the AI investment debate.

What would justify the optimism?

The bullish case becomes stronger if companies sustain demand, bring projects into service and demonstrate that financing remains manageable. Evidence of cancellations, repeated delays or worsening funding terms would support a more cautious interpretation.

The brokerages have made their call. The useful question now is whether the next company disclosures support it. A recovery in share prices can arrive quickly; proof that the underlying economics are improving takes numbers, execution and time.
