title: Should you leave Australia to avoid paying 47% tax on crypto gains?
summary: Some Australian crypto investors are moving overseas to avoid the huge CGT increase from July 2027. But there are also less drastic ways you can pay less tax.
content:
In part one of our special on how to avoid Australia’s massive hike in capital gains taxes on crypto in July next year, we looked at borrowing against your Bitcoin or setting up a self-managed super fund (SMSF), among four ways to mitigate the impact of the taxes.

While an SMSF offers Australians the greatest tax advantages, it’s only suitable for older investors, or those who are willing to lock up their crypto for decades until they retire. For younger investors, moving overseas could reduce your future crypto tax bills to 0% — but there are less drastic options to save on tax too. 

5. Leave Australia and move to country with 0% CGT

Australia’s impending tax changes have already inspired crypto king Fred Schebesta, founder of Finder.com, to become a tax exile in Singapore. 

From July, the top rate on real, long-term crypto gains will increase to 47%, minus the effects of inflation on the cost basis. 

For upwardly mobile, single crypto investors, the “nuclear option” of leaving the country to avoid giving almost half their gains to the government will look increasingly attractive.
Many of the world’s top crypto hubs — Singapore, Portugal, Malta, UAE and Hong Kong — offer 0% capital gains taxes on long-term crypto gains in an attempt to attract wealthy investors.

Also read: The one thing these 6 global crypto hubs all have in common...Should you leave Australia to avoid paying 47% tax on crypto gains?

Ben Simpson, founder of crypto advisory service Collective Shift, says some of his members have already pulled the trigger. 

“Yeah, we’ve had a number of people that have sort of packed up and gone basically, ‘f—- this. I’m off to the Bahamas or whatnot,’” he says. 

Andrea Yuen, CEO of Sywftx, says she is keenly aware of the tax advantages of living outside of Australia.

“I lived in Singapore for 30 years. I do miss my no capital gains tax,” she says. But she didn’t move there for tax reasons, and cautions that uprooting your life to avoid a bit of tax is a pretty drastic step.

“I would never say that we should structure our lives only to think about tax outcomes,” she says. “There are many other wonderful reasons why I’ve come back to Australia and continued to live in Australia.”

“I think if you’re moving countries solely based on a decision about whether you know your crypto is going to get taxed, then you probably need to think a little bit harder.” 

Simpson has considered the idea, given he already spends half the year in America looking after Collective Shift US, but looking into the rules put him off.

“You really have to cut pretty much all ties to Australia. So if you are genuinely happy to leave and don’t want to come back for the majority of the year, and cut your healthcare and cut all your ties back to Australia, then that is a strategy.” 

“Bitcoin Jesus” Roger Ver gave up his US residency in 2014, and ten years later he was arrested and charged over failing to correctly report the value of his crypto holdings and paying exit taxes. He was forced to pay almost $50 million to make the case go away.

Similarly, Australians leaving the country face a hefty exit tax on departure, which may require selling a decent amount of your stack.  

“They tax you on the way out. If you’ve got a lot of gains or profits you’re sitting on, they’ll catch you when you leave,” says Adrian Forza, director of Crypto Tax Australia. “Arguably it’d be bigger in the future, but it’s still difficult to stomach selling off everything to leave.”

Forza explains you also have the option of paying the Australian taxes later on, but on the full value of the gain after you sell the asset. So if you expect Bitcoin to go up, you’d be best off paying the exit tax now.

Related: Australia releases draft bill to adopt OECD crypto tax reporting framework

6. Set up a company to benefit from the company tax rate

Simpson is only 27 and the prospect of locking up his crypto portfolio for forty years holds little appeal. Instead, he trades and holds crypto via a company to benefit from the 25% company tax rate. 

Running a single-person company is easier than you might think, but not worth the hassle unless you have a reasonable amount of capital and intend to make a lot of trades. It requires registering the company with ASIC and paying an annual fee, paying an accountant to produce financial statements and/or an annual company tax return and mucking about with payroll software and payday superannuation contributions if you plan to pay yourself an income. You can pay yourself a dividend at any time when you need some money. 

“The company structure is good if you’re wanting to cap the capital gains tax at the company tax rate,” he says, but notes there’s a big catch: when you take funds out of the company, you need to pay the difference between the 25% company tax rate and your personal tax rate.

“You still need to pay your marginal income tax rates. If you’re on the top tax rate, like 47%,” he says.

You may be wondering: if you have to pay your income tax rate anyway, which will equal the CGT rate from July, what is the benefit in paying a few thousand dollars and filling out a bunch of paperwork to run a company?

Simpson explains that the key advantage is that while you are building up your crypto portfolio by trading in and out of different coins, you only pay the 25% company rate for each sale. That means paying up to 22% less than CGT each time you exit a position, which builds into an even more significant saving over time.

“Instead of paying 47% because you’ve just taken the profits… then the CGT amount is only 25% — the company tax rate. So when you put that money back in, you’ve got more capital to play with.”

However, if you don’t trade enough, it might be taxed at 30%.

Forza says the advantages are greater for those on higher incomes. 

“If you’re a single person, then you’ve got a company, and you’re earning, you know, 150 grand a year, um, or over 200, then yeah, definitely a company would be the way to go, especially now that the CGT discount has gone out the window.”

It’s not a particularly useful structure if you just plan to just hold your Bitcoin, however. There are some potential advantages but arguably not enough of them to be worth the hassle.

7. Just get out of crypto entirely to avoid high CGT rates

The 50% CGT discount has been replaced by an indexation discount, which takes into account how much inflation affects how much you paid originally for an asset. 

This means that investors who buy and hold dividend stocks or index funds for a long period will receive a bigger CGT discount. So should you drop crypto and buy a bunch of ETFs so you can pay less tax?

The short answer is no: the new CGT ‘discount’ is largely an illusion, as it simply measures your real gain after inflation.

Simpson says crypto has been hit hard by the CGT changes, but it still offers the best risk-reward opportunity.

“For us in Bitcoin, the growth ... heavily outweighs the tax considerations. In my point of view. If you’ve got the right portfolio, that can give you the right upside.”

History suggests that despite volatility and years-long bear markets, the return from investing in Bitcoin over time would still leave investors ahead of ETF investors even after paying more tax. Investing further down the risk curve with altcoins however, can either pay off handsomely or end in total disaster. 

JPMorgan assumes that Bitcoin will compound by 10% on average in the years ahead. (Source JPMorgan/Bitcoin Archive)

Simpson says he convinced his younger sister, who is a basketball player on a low income, to invest in Bitcoin two years ago rather than putting money into a savings account.

“She’s up like 40% or 50% in her portfolio and she’s like, ‘wow, this is going to get me so much further towards buying a house one day than sitting in cash and losing 10% [to inflation over time],” he says. 

“That’s why I think Bitcoin makes so much sense to accumulate. And the tax considerations are not really there for most people I think.”

Yuen says crypto is one of the few asset classes that offers investors the chance to make double-digit returns in a few months, or to potentially double their money. Even after paying the new taxes, crypto investors with those sorts of returns will still be ahead.

“My dad always said to me, it’s a good thing, if you’ve made profits, you should be happy to pay some tax on it.” 

Well maybe not happy about it, but you’ll still be making money.

Also read: How Aussie Bitcoiners can avoid 2027’s shock CGT hike, Part 1

title: Canton Hosts Tokenized US Share Trade Under SEC Innovation Exemption
summary: A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings…
content:
TL;DR: A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology.

A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology. The important development is not that a stock price was mirrored on a blockchain, but that the transaction was structured around the issuer, a transfer agent and verified holders.

How the transaction was structured

TSV says DRW Cumberland purchased tokenized Canton Strategic Holdings common stock from existing shareholder Five North. Fairmint, an SEC-registered transfer agent, recorded the shares in token form in a verified wallet, and Flowdesk provided liquidity. The parties describe this as the first trade of its kind under the SEC's innovation exemption. Because this is an operator announcement, the scope of that first-of-kind claim should be attributed to the participants. What can be identified concretely is the named issuer, the parties, the permissioned environment and the transfer-agent role in the share record.

Why actual shareholder rights matter

Tokenized equities can describe several very different products. Some are economic exposures issued by a separate intermediary; others aim to represent the issuer's shares with the rights and recordkeeping attached to conventional stock. Here the issuer-sponsored structure and transfer-agent involvement are central. They are intended to connect token holdings with the legally recognized ownership register, rather than just a derivative tracking a market price. Investors still need to know transfer restrictions, voting rights, eligibility rules and how corporate actions are administered. A blockchain token is not proof of all those protections by itself.

This is not open public share trading

The reported transactions occurred in a permissioned pool with verified participants. That is fundamentally different from announcing that any wallet can buy US shares without checks or through a decentralized exchange. Restricted access may be a design choice needed to satisfy securities obligations, investor eligibility and transfer controls. It may also limit liquidity and interoperability compared with the open token markets crypto users are accustomed to. The test of such infrastructure is whether these controls can function at scale without making trading and settlement more cumbersome than conventional systems.

The regulatory context remains narrow

The company referred to an SEC innovation exemption announced in September. The transaction should be read within the specific conditions of the applicable relief, not as proof the SEC has deregulated all tokenized securities. Different venues, issuers or instruments may require their own legal analysis. Reporting on this area is especially sensitive to the distinction between an operational pilot, a live limited transaction and a broadly available retail market. This appears to be the second category: a real transaction, but with explicit participation boundaries.

What a meaningful follow-up looks like

Future announcements should reveal the number and variety of issuers, whether transactions settle consistently, how ownership and voting are handled, and whether participants can transfer positions between approved venues. Costs, order-book depth and operational incidents will be more revealing than another first-trade headline. If tokenized US equities become a durable market structure, those unglamorous details will matter at least as much as the chain carrying the record.

Primary source: Tradecraft / TSV official announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s earlier report on transfer agents supporting tokenized securities.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: The $120 Billion Mirage: Penny Combos Inflated Prediction Market Volumes in Q3
summary:
Prediction markets celebrated a record $179.6 billion in trading volume in the third quarter. Still, a look beneath the headline figures reveals that actual capital deployed was less than a third of that total. 
 According to the data from Prediction Frontier, traders paid just $56.1 billion for tho...
content:
2026-11-09T22:52:00.000+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 20:52 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Four prediction venues recorded $179.6 billion in Q3 nominal volume, while buyers paid $56.1 billion for the contracts.
  • Kalshi combos contributed $67.1 billion in nominal volume, helping explain why headline turnover grew faster than purchase payments.

Prediction markets celebrated a record $179.6 billion in trading volume in the third quarter. Still, a look beneath the headline figures reveals that actual capital deployed was less than a third of that total.

According to the data from Prediction Frontier, traders paid just $56.1 billion for those contracts, with the massive $123 billion gap driven by how venues count low-cost multi-leg "combos."

The report, covering Kalshi, Polymarket’s international and US venues, and Novig, reflects the gap, created by the counting specifics: cheaper combinations of outcomes generate substantial payout-based volume from comparatively small purchases.

How $56 Billion Became $180 Billion

The report counts each traded contract at its $1 payout value, a convention Kalshi also uses in its reporting. Its alternative measure, “dollars paid”, multiplies the number of contracts by their execution price.

Buying 100 contracts for three cents each therefore produces $100 in nominal volume and $3 in purchase payments.

Combos widen the difference by combining several outcomes in one position. Under Kalshi’s rules, a combo pays $1 when every component settles at $1; any component settling at zero makes the whole contract worthless.

Low-priced combinations consequently generate more nominal volume per dollar spent on prediction markets.

Neither volume measure represents fresh deposits: contracts can trade repeatedly, and traders can reuse funds.

Kalshi’s Combos Widen the Gap

Kalshi combos accounted for $67.1 billion of quarterly nominal volume, which is more than a third of the four-venue total. On Kalshi, the average purchase payment per $1 contract fell from 32 cents in July to 24 cents in September.

Polymarket’s figure stayed near 50 cents. That changing mix matters when interpreting monthly records. Kalshi’s September nominal volume reached $60.7 billion, but dollars paid totalled $14.7 billion, just 10% above July, according to the report.

Across the tracked venues, nominal volume grew 84.3% quarter-on-quarter, against 54.7% growth in dollars paid. Nominal volume thus increased from about 2.7 times purchase payments in Q2 to 3.2 times in Q3.

The comparison includes expanded coverage, with Novig data beginning on August 4. Both measures rose in Q3, but their widening gap changes how the market’s records should be read.

For brokers comparing venues or gauging customer activity, nominal volume alone can obscure a shift toward cheaper contracts; dollars paid show whether purchase spending kept pace.

title: Bitcoin’s 6% Price Drop After $6.3B Binance Hack Signals Maturity: Fitch Ratings
summary: According to Fitch Ratings, bitcoin demonstrated growing market resilience following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, falling just 6%—a far milder price decline than those seen during previous crypto crises. Bitcoin’s Drop Defies Historical Market Sell-Offs Bitcoin’s market response to the massive Bin...
content:
1. News
  2. Featured
  3. Bitcoin's 6% Price Drop After $6.3B Binance Hack Signals Maturity: Fitch Ratings

Published:Nov 9, 2026, 3:50 PM EST

According to Fitch Ratings, bitcoin demonstrated growing market resilience following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, falling just 6%—a far milder price decline than those seen during previous crypto crises.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 9, 2026, 3:50 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • The price of bitcoin fell just 6% after the $6.3 billion Binance hack, outperforming its reaction to past crises.
  • Fitch Ratings cited a 67% trading volume surge as evidence of deeper liquidity and market maturity.
  • Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao urged industry unity as the breach highlighted ongoing cybersecurity risks.

Bitcoin’s Drop Defies Historical Market Sell-Offs

Bitcoin’s market response to the massive Binance hack demonstrated remarkable resilience, according to a report from Fitch Ratings, with the cryptocurrency holding up significantly better than during previous crises, including the COVID-19 sell-off.

The breach, which resulted in the theft of approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets across multiple blockchains, is considered the largest to date in the crypto industry. Among the stolen assets were roughly 18,270 bitcoin, valued at $1.5 billion at the time of the attack. Despite the scale of the breach and Binance’s temporary suspension of withdrawals and trading, bitcoin’s price fell only about 6% in the 10 hours following initial reports.

According to Fitch, the price reaction was far milder than declines recorded during previous market shocks. By comparison, bitcoin suffered a 35% single-day plunge at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020. The recent 6% decline was also considerably smaller than the 14% drop following the FTX collapse in 2022 and the 21% fall during the Bitstamp hack in 2015.

Fitch Ratings said the relatively contained price movement, coupled with a 67% surge in daily trading volume to $40.9 billion, signals a maturing cryptocurrency market structure.

“The lower level of disruption is probably due to crypto trading market structures having become deeper and more diversified,” Fitch stated. “Bitcoin’s increasingly diversified trading ecosystem reduces dependence on any single exchange and can support liquidity when individual venues are disrupted, even when it involves Binance.”

CZ Points to Market Resilience and Industry Unity

Days after the hack, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng “CZ” Zhao also highlighted bitcoin’s resilience while emphasizing the interconnected nature of digital asset markets. Calling for industry unity in the wake of the breach, Zhao argued that infighting within the Web3 ecosystem makes little sense when liquidity remains available across platforms.

He emphasized that despite the unprecedented scale of the breach, the broader crypto market’s interconnected structure helped prevent a systemic collapse. Zhao concluded that the industry must remain “decentralized but united” as its infrastructure matures.

Although Fitch cautioned that cybersecurity vulnerabilities and operational disruptions remain significant risks, the incident provided evidence of bitcoin’s growing market resilience. The cryptocurrency’s ability to withstand a severe exchange-specific shock without triggering a broader liquidity freeze or catastrophic price collapse suggests that market liquidity has become deeper and more diversified.

Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide
Europe's largest asset manager raised its Strategy holding to 1.9 million shares in the third quarter, a 13F shows, even as MSTR has since fallen about 18% from quarter-end.
This post Amundi Boosts Strategy (MS...
content:
Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices.

That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager.

The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show.

A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30.

Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides

Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456.

That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap.

MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. Since then the stock has tracked bitcoin’s slide into the mid-$70,000s, wiping out a large share of that mark-to-market gain for anyone still holding the Sept. 30 position.

The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. A weaker share price raises more dilution for every coin purchased, which is the feedback loop that has defined the stock’s moves this year.

Banks loaded bitcoin proxies in the same quarter

Amundi was not the only large European name adding bitcoin exposure on the quarter. Barclays’ own 13F, also filed Nov. 6, shows 3,942,900 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $186.7 million at Sept. 30, up 48% from 2,658,147 shares three months earlier, SEC records show.

That Barclays line carries the same caveat: a 13F gathers client, managed and trading book positions, not proof the bank put its own capital into bitcoin. Still, the two filings together sketch the same picture of Q3: traditional European managers kept adding exposure to bitcoin proxies even as the spot market cooled into the fall.

The institutional adds sit against a weaker tape since quarter-end. Bitcoin has slipped into the mid-$70,000s, Strategy stock has followed it down, and the value of Amundi’s disclosed MSTR stake has compressed even as the share count on the filing stayed fixed. At Monday’s close the disclosed stake was about $52 million below its Sept. 30 mark.

Whether Amundi kept buying, trimmed, or simply held through October’s slide will not show up until the next 13F. For now the Nov. 6 filing is the record Europe’s biggest asset manager left: nearly 1.9 million Strategy shares, up 44%, at a $291 million quarter-end mark.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Elizabeth Warren Plans Prediction Market Crackdown as She Prepares to Chair Senate Banking
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Elizabeth Warren Plans Prediction Market Crackdown as She Prepares to Chair Senate Banking
A Warren banking aide says the incoming Senate Banking chair will target prediction markets' "Wild West-style lack of oversight," after she and Sen. John Curtis pressed Kalshi and Polymarket ...
content:
Sen. Elizabeth Warren plans to crack down on prediction markets once she takes the Senate Banking Committee gavel in January, with a banking aide telling Punchbowl News that Warren would seek to stop the sector’s “Wild West-style lack of oversight.”

The Massachusetts Democrat is poised to chair the panel after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress last week, putting her in charge of a portfolio that covers banking, housing, the Federal Reserve and cryptocurrency. Punchbowl published the aide’s rundown of her agenda on Monday.

Warren intends to use the committee’s investigative powers for oversight of prediction markets and election betting platforms, aimed at insider trading and platform manipulation — the same fight she opened before the midterms.

That earlier push was bipartisan. On Oct. 28, Warren and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, wrote to Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour and Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan asking how the companies stop candidates, campaign staff and others with material nonpublic information from trading election contracts.

What Warren and Curtis asked Kalshi and Polymarket

“We are particularly troubled by election-related event contracts,” the senators wrote. “Event contracts tied to elections receive prominent coverage and are treated by some observers as indicators of political momentum. There are also documented cases of candidates betting on their own races, which undermines the overall integrity of the American electoral process.”

The letter cited candidates who traded on their own contests on Kalshi, including a February 2026 California gubernatorial race, and pointed to research alleging wash trading and volume manipulation on Polymarket. It also referenced an NPR investigation of campaign insiders who said they traded ahead of polling releases.

“The identification of isolated instances of improper trading does not demonstrate that these markets are adequately protected,” Warren and Curtis wrote. “Instead, it raises serious questions about how much similar activity may be going undetected.” They asked for written answers by Election Day, Nov. 3.

Kalshi’s head of enforcement, Robert DeNault, told Business Insider that the company “proactively blocks candidates and campaign staff from trading to protect market integrity.” Polymarket did not respond to that request for comment.

Crypto sits inside the same Banking gavel

Prediction markets are not a side show for bitcoin readers. Polymarket is a crypto-native venue that settled U.S. access through a CFTC-registered exchange after years offshore, while Kalshi operates as a designated contract market under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Both sit in the orbit of the same committee Warren is about to run.

Under Chairman Michael S. Selig, the CFTC has spent 2026 defending those platforms against state gambling laws, suing Wisconsin, New York and others to assert exclusive federal jurisdiction over event contracts on registered exchanges. A Democratic Banking chair targeting what her aide called a Wild West lands as the counterweight to that stance.

Warren has been one of crypto’s sharpest critics on the Hill. She opposed the CLARITY Act market structure bill, which failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15, and analysts have argued a Democratic Congress leaves little path for a Republican rewrite. House Democrats are already sketching their own package with a bigger SEC role.

The aide’s broader agenda for Warren also includes affordability legislation, a push to cap credit card interest rates, AI chip export controls, and oversight of Trump administration officials, Wall Street CEOs, Big Tech executives and anyone tied to the Trump family’s crypto ventures.

The test for prediction markets is no longer whether Trump-era regulators will keep clearing the way. It is whether Warren, with subpoena power and the Banking gavel, turns the Kalshi and Polymarket letter into hearings that rewrite how election and event contracts are policed.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic
summary: The blockchain firm traced stolen funds through six new tokens on NEAR, where hackers used liquidity pools to obscure transfers between wallets.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 9, 2026

The blockchain firm traced stolen funds through six new tokens on NEAR, where hackers used liquidity pools to obscure transfers between wallets.

North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch.

The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain.

How stolen NEAR moved between wallets through liquidity pools. Source: Elliptic

Elliptic also found that five of the six token creators were funded with proceeds from earlier token sales just two to 13 minutes before the next launch, linking the tokens in a chain of transactions.

“North Korea’s launderers rarely rely on a single technique,” Elliptic co-founder Tom Robinson wrote in the report. “Instead, they layer many cheap techniques, each adding a little more delay.”

Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

At the time of Elliptic’s analysis, about 11.8 million NEAR stolen in the Binance hack remained unmoved. Elliptic valued those funds at $43.7 million.

title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Launch With Faster AI and Lower Prices
summary: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cut API prices, but Ethan Mollick’s early tests show why stronger AI still needs human judgment.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cut API prices, but Ethan Mollick’s early tests show why stronger AI still needs human judgment.

Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, cutting standard API token prices by 20% and promising faster output as it pushes its most capable AI into more demanding coding, research and engineering work.

The company’s launch announcement on X describes the models as “designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.” The release is dated November 9 in Anthropic’s documentation and arrived on November 10 for New Zealand readers.

Fable and Mythos use the same underlying model, with different safeguards and access requirements.

Claude Fable 5.2 versus Mythos 5.2: who gets access?

According to Anthropic’s model documentation, Fable 5.2 targets demanding reasoning and lengthy agent sessions, including multistep research and work carried through to finished documents, spreadsheets or presentations. It supports a one-million-token context window and up to 128,000 output tokens.

Mythos shares its specifications and pricing but is restricted to organisations admitted through Anthropic’s verification programmes. The company directs cybersecurity and life-sciences researchers to the relevant access programmes.

Fable’s broader availability comes with stronger safeguards for cybersecurity and biology. The access split is therefore about permitted uses and misuse controls, not simply a cheaper model and a more expensive one.

Fable 5.2 is available through the Claude API and major cloud platforms, including Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. Availability and hosting arrangements vary by platform.

Lower prices, with a premium for speed

The published base rates are $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens for both models. Their 5.1 predecessors cost $10 and $50 respectively. That is a 20% reduction in each rate.

Chart: Brave New Coin. Source: Anthropic’s 5.2 documentation. Standard token rates only; fast mode, tools and other charges are excluded.

Anthropic says the new models generate output up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions. Its optional fast mode promises token generation at up to 2.5 times the speed, at $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens.

Those speed figures are company claims. The higher fast-mode price also means users should distinguish faster responses from cheaper completed work. Total costs depend on the amount of reasoning, the number of agents and the tools involved.

Beyond the chatbot: working electronic prototypes

A separate Anthropic research report offers a more tangible demonstration than a conversational benchmark. Working with circuit-board manufacturer Diode Computers, the company asked Fable 5.2 to design a USB speakerphone, a home voice-assistant hub and a handheld virtual pet.

Anthropic says Claude selected components, laid out circuit boards, designed enclosures and wrote firmware. Human engineers manufactured and assembled the devices under its guidance, and the prototypes worked without electrical modifications.

The practical limit matters: these are prototypes. Anthropic says they have not completed electrical validation, antenna tuning, thermal testing or certification, and were not designed for mass production. The demonstration shows progress in coordinating engineering tasks; commercial product readiness still requires further work.

What Anthropic’s coding benchmark shows

Chart: Anthropic, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 announcement. FrontierCode 2.0 coding accuracy versus cost per task; the cost axis is logarithmic. Results are vendor-reported and depend on the stated evaluation settings.

Anthropic’s FrontierCode 2.0 evaluation gives Fable 5.2 a 49.1% score at Xhigh effort, versus 32.4% for Fable 5.1 at that setting. The chart also shows Fable 5.2 scoring 45.3% at High effort, close to Opus 5.5’s 45.5% at Max, for roughly half the cost per task.

There is an important wrinkle: Fable 5.2’s more expensive Max setting scores below Xhigh on this evaluation. More spending does not automatically produce a better result. These are Anthropic’s evaluation results, with specific settings and methods; users still need to test their own workloads.

Why Ethan Mollick calls it “Jagged AGI”

Early hands-on testing raises a more revealing question: can the model recognise when its own work has gone off course? In Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI, entrepreneurship professor Ethan Mollick describes near-expert performance across many computer-based tasks. He describes it as “almost” artificial general intelligence (AGI), under a limited definition that excludes many human tasks and most jobs.

One creative project became bogged down after agent teams built an 87,500-word rulebook. “The AI had built a bureaucracy,” he wrote. Human intervention and a separate team of AI reviewers helped untangle the process. He also stopped a business-building experiment at the demonstration stage, without establishing that the AI could run it independently.

The distinction is between producing impressive work and recognising whether it is useful, proportionate and finished. For business buyers, that makes human review and coordination costs part of the productivity calculation. Mollick disclosed free prerelease usage, while saying he takes no money from AI labs and has no financial interest in Anthropic’s IPO.

The upgrade has compatibility and privacy conditions

Developers moving from 5.1 face changes beyond a new model name. Anthropic’s upgrade documentation warns that editing earlier conversation history can invalidate retained reasoning blocks. An older computer-use interface also fails on most platforms, with an Amazon Bedrock exception. Existing integrations need testing before a production switch.

Enterprise privacy is another purchasing consideration. Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards architecture allows monitoring data to be stored in infrastructure controlled by the customer, with review signals routed to that customer’s team. Access and deployment conditions still need to be checked for each organisation.

The model documentation specifies 30-day data retention unless Anthropic expressly authorises a zero-data-retention arrangement. For banks, trading firms and other organisations handling sensitive material, that is a deployment condition to establish before connecting the model to internal systems.

The launch follows BNC’s coverage of Anthropic’s power commitments and IPO valuation pressure. Lower unit prices and more ambitious uses sharpen the commercial question: can customers obtain enough useful work from increasingly capable models to justify the infrastructure behind them?

For users evaluating 5.2 now, the meaningful test is a completed task at an acceptable cost, with the right access and data controls—not the model name alone.

title: Bitcoin CPI Preview: Three Tests for a Fragile Crypto Market
summary: Bitcoin faces October’s US inflation report with prices under pressure, a divided Federal Reserve and investors looking beyond the headline number for signs of relief.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH

Bitcoin faces October’s US inflation report with prices under pressure, a divided Federal Reserve and investors looking beyond the headline number for signs of relief.

Bitcoin is approaching the October US inflation release with more to prove than whether it can bounce on a favourable number. Prices have fallen to their weakest levels in more than two months, the Federal Reserve is divided over whether rates should rise, and crypto investors are also digesting a changed political landscape.

This Bitcoin CPI preview focuses on three tests: what the inflation report actually says, whether it changes the interest-rate outlook, and whether any improvement survives the market’s first burst of trading.

The report is scheduled for November 10 at 8:30 a.m. US Eastern, covering October prices. That is 1:30 p.m. UTC, or 2:30 a.m. on November 11 in New Zealand. The figures had not been released when this preview was prepared.

Bitcoin CPI preview: why the starting point matters

Reuters reported on November 9 that Bitcoin fell more than 2% to $73,708, its lowest since August. That is a dated market observation, rather than a live price or a technical floor.

The report linked the fall to concern about tougher cryptocurrency regulation under a Democratic-controlled Congress. It also described sentiment damaged by the major Binance theft. Inflation is therefore arriving in a market carrying several sources of uncertainty, rather than one waiting on a single economic statistic.

A cooler report could remove one pressure without resolving the others. Equally, a hotter reading would arrive before investors have fully digested the recent political and market shocks.

Test one: look past the annual headline

The previous Bureau of Labor Statistics release showed headline consumer prices rising 3.7% over the year to September, up from 3.4% in August. Monthly headline inflation accelerated to 0.6% from 0.4%.

Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in September and accounted for more than half the monthly headline increase. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% over the month and 2.6% over the year.

That split matters. An easing of fuel pressure can improve headline inflation while leaving underlying price increases less reassuring. October’s core reading and the contribution from shelter will help show whether improvement extends beyond energy.

Chart: Brave New Coin, using BLS September 2026 CPI data, Table A. These are historical figures; October’s results are still pending.

The distinction between a lower inflation rate and falling prices also matters for readers. A slowdown means prices are rising less quickly; it does not necessarily reverse the increases households have already absorbed.

Test two: does the number change the Fed debate?

The Fed’s October 28 decision held its target range at 3.75%–4%, with a 10–2 vote. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase.

“Inflation remains elevated,” the committee said, adding that more information would help determine the appropriate stance of policy. The two dissents underline why a lower headline number cannot simply be treated as a signal that cuts are imminent.

For Bitcoin, the connection runs through the wider market’s assessment of financial conditions. Changes in expected interest rates affect the appeal of cash and bonds, financing costs and investors’ willingness to own volatile assets. That mechanism can matter even though Bitcoin’s supply rules do not change with the CPI release.

One report also cannot dictate the next decision. The Fed’s next scheduled meeting is December 8–9, leaving further information to arrive before policymakers vote again.

The useful question is therefore whether the data materially changes the balance of risks facing the committee. A report that looks better than September could still leave inflation high enough to keep policymakers cautious.

Test three: can Bitcoin hold the reaction?

The initial price move will give readers a headline. What happens after that will provide a more useful assessment of whether the market has changed its view.

Three observations can help: whether Treasury yields and the dollar support the same interpretation of the inflation news, whether strength is shared across other risk assets, and whether Bitcoin retains its move after the first wave of orders.

These are checks on the market’s interpretation, not a guaranteed trading formula. Bitcoin can move for cryptocurrency-specific reasons while equities or bonds respond to the economic release differently. A brief spike is not, by itself, evidence that the broader downturn has ended.

For the same reason, comparing the published figures with a current, clearly sourced consensus will be essential once the report arrives. Improvement from the previous month and a positive surprise relative to expectations are different claims.

A report can clear one test and fail another. Lower annual headline inflation alongside stubborn monthly core inflation would offer a mixed signal. A favourable reading followed by a short-lived Bitcoin bounce would also demand a different account from one accompanied by sustained buying. Reporting the details separately will make the eventual verdict more useful.

A preview now, a verdict after the release

BNC’s earlier coverage examined Bitcoin’s CPI test following the AI stock sell-off. The next step is to match the new inflation details to observable market behaviour, rather than force the result into a predetermined bullish or bearish story.

A convincing improvement would need more than a comforting headline: broader evidence of easing inflation, a meaningful shift in the rate debate and a market response that lasts. Until the October figures arrive, those remain tests to watch—not results to declare.

title: Formation Securities plans Solana stock trading venue under SEC exemption
summary: The proposed venue would offer 24/7 trading of tokenized shares from Galaxy Digital, Exodus and Forward Industries, with a launch planned for early 2027.
content:
Formation Securities, a newly established company licensing technology from decentralized exchange Orca, has notified the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) of plans to launch a tokenized stock trading venue on Solana in early 2027.

The company said Monday that tokenized shares of Galaxy Digital, Exodus Movement and Forward Industries are expected to be available at launch. The venue would operate under the SEC’s temporary Innovation Exemption announced in September, which allows verified investors to trade certain US-listed shares around the clock while retaining voting, dividend and other shareholder rights.

Superstate and Securitize are expected to make tokenized shares available on the marketplace, which Formation says it intends to develop in cooperation with public companies. The venue would use automated market maker (AMM) technology, allowing investors to hold securities in their own wallets and settle trades onchain against stablecoins and other eligible assets.

Traditional transfer agents would continue to maintain official shareholder records, preserving companies’ direct relationships with shareholders.

Solana is already among the largest blockchains for tokenized equities, with approximately $575 million in tokenized stock value as of Monday, compared with $747 million on Ethereum and $1.7 billion on BNB Chain, according to RWA.xyz data.

Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

Tokenized stock plans draw issuer concerns

Formation’s issuer-focused approach comes amid growing debate over how publicly traded shares should be brought onchain. As of early November, more than 50 companies had objected to having their shares tokenized on OKXICE, a proposed venue backed by crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange.

Under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, trading venues must notify issuers in writing and wait at least 30 calendar days before trading shares tokenized by unaffiliated third parties, giving companies an opportunity to object. Nasdaq warned in September that tokenized stock trading could have unforeseen consequences for liquidity, price discovery and long-term shareholder value.

title: Trump Crypto Firms Face Senate Records Deadline as Democrats Prepare to Take Control
summary: Trump-linked crypto businesses, Binance and Tether face renewed Senate demands for records as Richard Blumenthal prepares to take charge of an investigative panel.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BNB TRUMP USDT WLFI

Trump-linked crypto businesses, Binance and Tether face renewed Senate demands for records as Richard Blumenthal prepares to take charge of an investigative panel.

Trump crypto firms are facing a deadline with a different political weight behind it. Senator Richard Blumenthal has renewed demands for records from World Liberty Financial and the company behind the TRUMP memecoin, alongside Binance and Tether, as Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate.

The November 5 announcement sets January 4, 2027, as the final date for voluntary production. The senator’s office identifies him as the incoming chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. An inquiry pursued from the minority is moving towards a committee room he expects to run.

That is the pressure point: companies that have disputed the allegations or resisted document demands now face a change in who controls the investigation.

Trump crypto firms face a three-date countdown

Blumenthal’s letter to Fight Fight Fight LLC, addressed to Bill Zanker, asks the company to confirm receipt by November 9 and begin producing records by November 30. Further material is to follow on a schedule agreed with committee staff.

If records are not voluntarily supplied by January 4, the panel would consider “alternative measures to obtain compliance,” he wrote.

The dates turn a long-running dispute into a practical test of cooperation. These are requests for documents, however, rather than findings of wrongdoing. The November letters do not themselves establish that a subpoena has been issued or that any recipient broke the law.

Graphic: Brave New Coin. Dates from the November 5 Senate letter to Binance and the corresponding Fight Fight Fight request. The letters do not constitute findings of wrongdoing.

Behind the memecoin: who owns it, who paid, who benefited?

The Fight Fight Fight packet includes Blumenthal’s original May 2025 request. It seeks ownership and management information, financial relationships with Trump-associated businesses, revenue from the token and policies addressing potential conflicts of interest.

It also asks for records about the dinner promotion for leading TRUMP holders, including registration information, communications and arrangements surrounding a previously advertised White House tour. That makes the inquiry about the business machinery behind the spectacle: how token ownership, payments and access were connected.

There is an obvious human tension in that material. A coin promoted through the president’s name attracted buyers seeking everything from speculative gains to proximity to power. Investigators want records that could distinguish the marketing from the money trail.

World Liberty Financial is a separate recipient of the renewed demands. Blumenthal’s office says the inquiry into the Trump-linked ventures began in May 2025 and concerns possible ethics violations, foreign financial relationships and conflicts of interest.

World Liberty has previously disputed suggestions that its business influenced administration policy. In an April 13 report, the Associated Press said the company denied any connection between a UAE investment and the president’s policy on chip sales. That was a response to earlier conflict-of-interest allegations, rather than the new records demand.

Binance disputes the allegations behind its inquiry

The exchange’s case has its own paper trail. In his November 5 letter to Binance chief executive Richard Teng, Blumenthal renewed February and April requests concerning anti-money-laundering policies and practices. He accused the exchange of failing to provide an adequate response and responsive records.

Binance has offered a sharply different account. Its March 6 response called the reporting behind the earlier inquiry “false, unsupported, and defamatory” and said its investigations of Hexa Whale and Blessed Trust followed law-enforcement enquiries.

The company said it removed both entities from its platform, prohibited users located in Iran and had more than 1,500 compliance specialists. It also denied dismissing staff for raising compliance concerns.

Those are the company’s statements about the earlier allegations, rather than a new answer to the November deadline. The disagreement now includes both the underlying transactions and whether Binance supplied enough evidence to substantiate its account.

Tether received a separate renewed demand. Blumenthal’s office links that inquiry to illicit cryptocurrency use and alleged dealings involving the administration. Those accusations remain the senator’s; a document request is not proof of the conduct alleged.

A new Congress changes the leverage

CoinDesk’s post-election assessment describes an industry adjusting to Democratic control of both chambers after two years of a much friendlier environment in Washington. Committee control matters even when passing legislation remains difficult: oversight can bring executives, correspondence and business arrangements into public view.

The companies involved also occupy different corners of crypto. An exchange, a stablecoin issuer, a finance venture and a presidential memecoin do not share one business model. Their inclusion in the same announcement does not make the accusations against them interchangeable.

For market participants, the immediate question is what documents emerge and what they establish. Political confrontation alone cannot answer that. Nor should a change in committee leadership be presented as an automatic change in cryptocurrency law.

There is also a distinction between providing a public explanation and supplying the underlying material investigators requested. A company can reject an accusation in a statement while a committee continues to seek contracts, communications or transaction records. That gap between competing accounts and supporting documents is where the next phase of this dispute will be fought.

What happens next

The next visible milestones are company responses, the start of production on November 30 and the January deadline. Any announcement of further compulsory action would be a separate development.

The scrutiny also arrives while investors face Bitcoin’s inflation test after the AI stock sell-off. Crypto’s Washington relationships and its exposure to broader financial conditions are being tested at the same time.

Blumenthal has supplied the countdown. Whether it produces meaningful disclosure, another confrontation or both will depend on what the companies actually hand over.

  • Eligible US retail clients can now trade SOL, AVAX and LINK alongside Bitcoin and Ether through Schwab Crypto.
  • Trading requires a separate crypto account linked to a Schwab brokerage account, with a 0.75% fee on each purchase or sale.

Schwab Crypto has added Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink alongside Bitcoin and Ether, bringing its supported cryptocurrencies to five. Eligible retail clients can buy and sell SOL, AVAX and LINK against the US dollar from November 9, Charles Schwab announced.

The US brokerage first announced plans for the three additions in August. Their launch follows the broader rollout of Schwab Crypto, which began with early access for small groups of customers in May. Bitcoin and Ether trading became available to all eligible retail clients in October.

The service operates in all US states except New York and Louisiana, with US territories and international jurisdictions also excluded.

Separate Accounts, a 0.75% Trading Fee

Clients use a separate Schwab Crypto account offered by Charles Schwab Premier Bank, SSB, linked to an eligible Schwab brokerage account.

They can fund it by moving available cash from the linked brokerage account. Schwab charges 0.75% of the value of each purchase or sale, with a minimum fee of $0.01.

Clients can view and trade their crypto holdings alongside traditional investments through Schwab.com, Schwab Mobile and thinkorswim. Schwab’s account terms also provide for round-the-clock customer support.

Under the custody arrangements outlined at launch, Charles Schwab Premier Bank safeguards clients’ digital assets and maintains ownership records, while Paxos provides sub-custody and trade execution.

Cryptocurrency holdings are not covered by FDIC insurance or SIPC protection.

Adding Direct Ownership to Existing Crypto Exposure

Schwab’s customers already had several ways to invest in digital assets before spot trading launched. These included crypto ETPs and futures, options on spot crypto ETPs, and funds investing in the wider digital asset sector.

In its April launch announcement, Schwab estimated that its clients held approximately 20% of spot crypto ETPs. That company estimate referred to holdings of exchange-traded products, not direct ownership of cryptocurrencies.

The spot service adds direct crypto holdings to those existing investment routes. Charles Schwab described the launch as a way for customers to conduct more of their financial activities with the firm and eventually bring existing digital assets onto its platform.

That transfer capability is now being introduced gradually. According to Schwab’s current FAQ, clients can send and receive supported cryptocurrencies once their accounts have been enabled and they have enrolled in transfers.

title: Mercado Bitcoin begins post-hack reopening without a timeline for withdrawals
summary: Customers can view their pre-hack balances as access returns in phases. The exchange has yet to say when withdrawals will resume.
content:
Crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin began restoring read-only access to customer accounts in phases on Monday, a week after attackers drained an estimated $49 million from the platform. The exchange has yet to say when customers will be able to withdraw funds.

A Mercado Bitcoin spokesperson told Cointelegraph that access would begin at 19:00 UTC, with all accounts expected to be viewable by 21:00 UTC. Customers will be able to see their holdings as they stood on Nov. 2, the day of the hack.

In a video posted to the exchange’s X account, Fabricio Tota, vice president of new business, said Mercado Bitcoin hoped read-only access would reassure customers that their assets were still recorded on the platform.

Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest crypto exchanges, told Brazilian magazine Veja in late October that it had more than 4.8 million customers and had processed over 215 billion Brazilian reais ($39 billion) in cumulative transactions. The exchange says it is using its own funds to replace the stolen assets, but has yet to give a date for withdrawals to resume.

“A more conservative approach”

Tota explained that the company opted for “a more conservative approach” to reactivating accounts “to ensure our return happens with the utmost security.” The caution follows concerns from blockchain security analysts that the attackers were able to access addresses, draining funds through standard transfers rather than a smart contract exploit. 

Blockchain analysts traced some of the stolen funds to customer deposit addresses, but Mercado Bitcoin says customers won’t bear the losses. “The vast majority of assets, in fact, nearly all of them, were never even touched by anyone; they were not even involved in the incident,” Tota said in the video. 

On Nov. 4, Mercado Bitcoin pledged to cover all losses with company funds, bolstered by a $20 million investment from stablecoin issuer Tether in July. Tota highlighted that a portion of the stolen funds were also frozen in the hours after the company announced an attack had taken place. 

The road to full recovery

The next phase of recovery will require users to confirm their registration details on the platform before they can move funds. The exchange plans to restore withdrawals via Pix, Brazil’s instant payment system, initially allowing customers to withdraw only to accounts in their own name. Tota gave no date for either step.

Mercado Bitcoin has yet to explain how the attackers gained access to its wallets. Blockchain data company Bitquery found that as of Nov. 4, wallets it linked to the attacker held most of the stolen funds that had escaped freezes, including 106.07 BTC.

title: PNC Bank tests turning USDC payments into dollar deposits
summary: The pilot lets eligible corporate and institutional clients accept USDC on Ethereum, with each token converted to one US dollar before deposit.
content:
PNC Bank, the eighth-largest US bank by assets, launched a limited pilot enabling eligible corporate and institutional clients to receive USDC payments through Coinbase.

The pilot accepts USDC, a US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Circle, on Ethereum using Coinbase Payments products. Payments are automatically converted into dollars and deposited into designated PNC accounts, allowing businesses to accept stablecoins without holding them.

PNC said the service aims to speed up access to funds and improve cross-border payment efficiency. The bank did not disclose fees, settlement-time benchmarks or the number of participating clients, nor did it respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details by publication time.

The pilot builds on a partnership established in July 2025, when PNC agreed to offer cryptocurrency services through Coinbase’s infrastructure while providing banking services to the exchange. The partnership led to the launch of Bitcoin (BTC) trading for eligible PNC Private Bank clients in December.

PNC’s move follows a similar initiative by Citi, which expanded its Coinbase partnership in September to enable institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments through its Spring by Citi platform, with Coinbase converting the payments into fiat currency.

USDC is the second-largest stablecoin by market capitalization, at $70.5 billion, behind Tether’s USDT at $176.8 billion, according to DefiLlama data. The total stablecoin market stood at around $290.8 billion on Monday.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: Glassnode Flags Rising Hyperliquid Whale Shorts as BTC Breaks Below 50-Week MA
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) is facing renewed selling pressure as large traders on Hyperliquid increase bearish bets, while the weekly close below a key long-term moving average raises concerns about further downside.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) is facing renewed selling pressure as large traders on Hyperliquid increase bearish bets, while the weekly close below a key long-term moving average raises concerns about further downside.

On-chain data from Glassnode shows a significant shift in whale positioning, adding to an increasingly cautious technical outlook.

BTC traded near $74,704 on Bitstamp, down approximately 1.45% at the latest available reading. The decline followed a weekly close around $74,968, below the 50-week moving average (MA), which stood between approximately $75,200 and $75,500. The move ended a seven-week streak above the indicator and marked Bitcoin’s first weekly close below it in roughly two months.

Glassnode Shows Hyperliquid Whales Increasing Bitcoin Shorts

Glassnode data indicates that large traders on Hyperliquid have shifted their Bitcoin perpetual futures positioning from net long to net short. The change occurred approximately two weeks ago, ending a seven-month period during which these traders maintained a predominantly bullish position.

Hyperliquid whales have increased Bitcoin perpetual shorts, flipping their net positioning short two weeks ago after seven months long. Source: Glassnode via X

The 24-hour mean net positioning metric, which measures the difference between long and short exposure, shows that bearish positions have continued to increase. Short exposure has now reached its highest level since October 2025.

The historical comparison adds another layer of concern. The last time Hyperliquid whales maintained a comparable level of short exposure, Bitcoin experienced a considerable price decline. Although historical positioning does not establish that another selloff will follow, the latest data highlights growing caution among large derivatives traders.

The shift also coincides with Bitcoin’s failure to maintain support above the 50-week MA. Together, the derivatives positioning and weakening price structure suggest that large traders are becoming more defensive as the market searches for support.

Bitcoin Price Breaks Below 50-Week Moving Average

Bitcoin’s weekly close near $74,968 placed the asset below its 50-week MA, estimated at $75,200–$75,500. According to market commentary shared by AshCrypto, the breakdown ended a seven-week period above the indicator.

Bitcoin closed the week at approximately $74,968, breaking below the 50-week MA for the first time in two months and ending a seven-week streak above it. Source: @AshCrypto via X

The 50-week MA is closely watched because it provides a reference for Bitcoin’s longer-term trend. Previous market cycles have shown that sustained trading below this level can coincide with extended periods of weakness. However, temporary breaches have also occurred without establishing new cycle lows.

AshCrypto outlined two possible developments following the latest breakdown. A quick recovery above the 50-week MA during the current week could turn the move into a bullish fakeout, potentially trapping traders who entered short positions during the decline.

Conversely, another weekly close below the indicator would strengthen the bearish technical picture. Under that scenario, Bitcoin could face additional selling pressure, with the low-$60,000 region emerging as a potential downside area.

Historical comparisons from the 2011–2012 and 2019–2020 market cycles offer some context. In both periods, Bitcoin experienced dips below the 50-week MA after reclaiming the indicator without subsequently establishing new cycle lows. BTC is currently around 26% above its June 2026 low of $59,517.

BTC Technical Indicators Show Broad Selling Pressure

TradingView’s latest technical summary gives Bitcoin an overall Sell rating. Moving averages account for most of the negative readings, with 12 Sell signals, one Neutral signal, and two Buy signals. Oscillators present a more mixed picture, although the combined technical assessment remains bearish.

The aggregate reading stands at 13 Sell, seven Neutral, and six Buy signals. This suggests that the prevailing trend remains negative despite signs that some short-term momentum indicators are approaching oversold conditions.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 36, placing it below the midpoint of its range but above the conventional oversold threshold of 30. Meanwhile, the Stochastic indicator has fallen to 14, the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) stands at -127, and Williams Percent Range has reached -85. All three readings indicate stretched downside momentum and generate Buy signals under the TradingView methodology.

However, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains negative at -1,709, maintaining a Sell signal. This divergence suggests that short-term selling pressure has become extended, but the broader momentum structure has yet to show a convincing recovery.

Bitcoin also trades below most of its key short- and medium-term moving averages. The 10-day EMA stands near $76,573, while the 20-day EMA is around $78,050. The 50-day EMA is approximately $79,209, placing several resistance levels above the current market price.

The 200-day simple moving average (SMA), near $73,153, remains an important longer-term reference. BTC is still trading above this level, leaving some room for the market to stabilize before testing deeper support.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: Key Support and Resistance Levels

Bitcoin’s immediate technical structure points to the $73,300–$73,150 region as an important support zone. This area combines the classic pivot S1 near $73,329 with the 200-day SMA around $73,153.

A sustained move below this confluence could expose the next downside level near $69,227, corresponding to the classic pivot S2. Further weakness could bring the broader $60,000 region into focus, particularly if Bitcoin records another weekly close below the 50-week MA.

On the upside, the first resistance area sits between approximately $76,500 and $78,500. This range includes the 10-day and 20-day moving averages, which Bitcoin would need to reclaim to improve its short-term technical structure.

A stronger recovery toward $79,200–$80,274 would encounter another resistance cluster, including the 50-day EMA and the classic central pivot. Reclaiming these levels would provide additional evidence that buyers are regaining control.

For now, Glassnode’s derivatives data, the weekly moving-average breakdown, and TradingView’s broader Sell rating point to continued caution. A recovery above the 50-week MA would weaken the immediate bearish signal, while another weekly close below it would keep lower support levels in focus.

title: North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot
Elliptic says North Korean launderers created six throwaway meme tokens on NEAR between Nov. 5 and 7, moving about $430,000 of stolen Binance funds through homemade liquidity pools.
This post North Korea Is Mint...
content:
North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote.

The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved.

“Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.”

How the homemade token trick works

The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset.

At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit.

Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Each was traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR and then abandoned. None has traded since Nov. 8, and that afternoon the creators of four of them withdrew what liquidity was left. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain.

Elliptic first reported the same approach in the laundering of the February 2025 Bybit theft, also attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, when a worthless Tron token helped move at least $24 million. In the Binance case the firm has also seen the technique on Tron and a close variant on Solana that used existing thinly traded tokens rather than homemade ones.

A slowing tactic, not a disappearing act

The meme coins do not hide the funds. Every step is public on-chain. What they buy is time. Each extra hop slows investigators while launderers race to move funds before they are flagged, and at about $90 apiece the tokens are cheap enough to throw away.

That fits the larger pattern Elliptic has tracked since the theft: more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions. Binance has said the attack began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before any coins moved. Blockchain firms linked the breach to TraderTraitor within a day.

The conversion into bitcoin is the bigger dollar story. All of the stolen SOL has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, and much of the XRP route has fed into bitcoin as well. About $2.85 billion of the original haul has been frozen. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far, Elliptic said.

North Korea’s crypto theft machine is not new. Elliptic put the North Korean regime’s 2025 haul above $2 billion, driven by the $1.46 billion Bybit exploit, and its cumulative known total above $6 billion even before Binance.

Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it covered customer losses from its own funds. The test for investigators is whether homemade liquidity pools keep multiplying faster than the blocklists catching up to them.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: EU Wants Market Participants to Write Their Own Tokenisation Rulebook
summary:
The European Central Bank, European Commission, and ESMA want banks and tech vendors to come up with unified settlement and custody rules well before proposed EU laws formally mandate them.

Applications close on November 27, 2026, with work expected to begin in January 2027, according to the call f...
content:
2026-11-09T19:10:00.000+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 17:10 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • An industry-led group will develop standards for holding and settling tokenised securities across DLT platforms and existing infrastructure.
  • Work is expected to begin in January 2027, before proposed EU reforms become law, with initial standards targeted for early 2028.

The European Central Bank, European Commission, and ESMA want banks and tech vendors to come up with unified settlement and custody rules well before proposed EU laws formally mandate them.

The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority opened nominations for the European Tokenisation Standards Group on November 9.

Applications close on November 27, 2026, with work expected to begin in January 2027, according to the call for nominations.

Common Standards for Holding and Settlement

The group will review existing European and international tokenisation standards, identify gaps and determine where additional rules are needed, according to its mandate.

Its work will cover both connections between distributed ledger technology platforms and links between those networks and existing financial infrastructure.

Once standards are agreed, members will develop a framework to monitor their implementation. They may also recommend measures for EU authorities to encourage adoption.

Industry representatives will chair the group and seek agreement through consensus, while the ECB, Commission and ESMA will participate as permanent observers.

Membership is open to financial firms, industry associations and technology providers, among other stakeholders. Nominees must represent organisations with a European presence and bring relevant experience in financial standards.

Work Begins Before the Legislative Requirement

The authorities want tokenisation standardisation work to start before lawmakers complete proposed changes to the DLT Pilot Regime. The group is already being formed; the legislative requirement for industry cooperation remains a proposal.

The Commission’s December 2025 Market Integration and Supervision Package would require participants in the post-trading chain, both within the pilot and beyond it, to work towards interoperability and supporting technical standards.

The existing DLT Pilot Regime, applicable since March 2023, allows authorised operators to run trading and settlement infrastructure for tokenised financial instruments with specific regulatory exemptions.

The group aims to deliver its first standards supporting Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative for an integrated tokenised financial ecosystem, by early 2028, according to its mandate.

Applications close on November 27, 2026, with work expected to begin in January 2027, according to the call for nominations.

Common Standards for Holding and Settlement

The group will review existing European and international tokenisation standards, identify gaps and determine where additional rules are needed, according to its mandate.

Its work will cover both connections between distributed ledger technology platforms and links between those networks and existing financial infrastructure.

Once standards are agreed, members will develop a framework to monitor their implementation. They may also recommend measures for EU authorities to encourage adoption.

Industry representatives will chair the group and seek agreement through consensus, while the ECB, Commission and ESMA will participate as permanent observers.

Membership is open to financial firms, industry associations and technology providers, among other stakeholders. Nominees must represent organisations with a European presence and bring relevant experience in financial standards.

Work Begins Before the Legislative Requirement

The authorities want tokenisation standardisation work to start before lawmakers complete proposed changes to the DLT Pilot Regime. The group is already being formed; the legislative requirement for industry cooperation remains a proposal.

The Commission’s December 2025 Market Integration and Supervision Package would require participants in the post-trading chain, both within the pilot and beyond it, to work towards interoperability and supporting technical standards.

The existing DLT Pilot Regime, applicable since March 2023, allows authorised operators to run trading and settlement infrastructure for tokenised financial instruments with specific regulatory exemptions.

The group aims to deliver its first standards supporting Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative for an integrated tokenised financial ecosystem, by early 2028, according to its mandate.
