title: TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress
TD Cowen's Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on a congressional ban on platform stablecoin yield over the next two years, even as banks renew their push after Democratic midterm wins.
This p...
content:
Banks will try again to stop crypto platforms from paying yield on stablecoin balances, but TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on Congress enacting such a ban over the next two years, he wrote in a Monday policy note shared with Bitcoin Magazine and clients.

The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban.

His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep.

A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path.

Why Seiberg still sees a path

That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted.

It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%.

Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill.

Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks.

There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors.

What GENIUS already banned, and what it left open

The fight is leftover business from the GENIUS Act, which President Trump signed on July 18, 2025, as Public Law 119-27. The statute bars permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers from paying “any form of interest or yield” solely for holding, using or retaining a payment stablecoin.

It does not explicitly cover exchanges and other intermediaries. That gap is what banks call the loophole. The American Bankers Association and state bankers associations urged Congress late last year to treat platform rewards as banned interest, and the ABA and Independent Community Bankers of America later pressed the Senate to harden Clarity language against balance- and tenure-based rewards. ICBA has warned that yield-bearing payment stablecoins could pull deposits from community banks and cut local lending.

Stablecoins are the main trading pair for bitcoin on most exchanges, so the yield fight lands on how bitcoin markets settle and how platforms attract dollar balances. The OCC’s final GENIUS rules, effective in January 2027, left the third-party rewards question for case-by-case review after banks had hoped the agency would close it.

House Democrats are already sketching their own market structure approach with a bigger SEC role. Seiberg’s note treats a narrow yield ban as the one bank ask that might still clear 60 votes even if Clarity does not.

The reason the odds are not zero, he wrote, is that community banks are effective at arguing that stablecoin yields pull funds out of banks and hurt local lending, and small banks have a record of getting Congress to act. He remains dubious.

The test for the next Congress is whether banks can peel yield off the broader crypto fight, or whether Democratic splits and the retail-investor optics keep the probability where Seiberg put it Monday: one in ten.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT
BlackRock's Robbie Mitchnick told Barron's demand to swap directly held bitcoin for IBIT shares is at its highest yet, with "security and peace of mind" the top reason as kidnappings and hacks rise.
This post BlackRock:...
content:
Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list.

“The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s, adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.”

The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size.

Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025.

In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.”

He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said.

How BlackRock’s swaps became possible

The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024.

Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported.

Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.”

Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6.

Why the flow numbers overstate demand

An in-kind creation adds IBIT shares and counts toward the fund’s reported flows, but no bitcoin is bought on the open market. The coins already existed and simply changed wrappers, so headline flow figures overstate new cash.

Cash has been moving the other way. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28 billion in the week ended Nov. 6, their worst week since June, and IBIT accounted for about $1.21 billion of that, Farside Investors data shows.

Self-custody under pressure

The fears behind the trade are documented. French authorities have recorded 77 crypto-linked kidnappings, extortion cases and home invasions so far in 2026, more than in all of 2025, the OCCRP reported, citing the national organized crime prosecutor. Reuters reported last year that Ledger’s co-founder lost a finger after being kidnapped with his wife.

The U.S. has its own cases, including a failed Connecticut plot to force a family to hand over bitcoin. Bitcoin security researcher Jameson Lopp maintains a public list of physical attacks on holders dating back to 2014, and the Coldcard bug in August put hardware wallets under scrutiny too.

The shift cuts against bitcoin’s founding pitch of holding money without a bank. Holders who convert give up their private keys for a brokerage claim, trading the risk of guarding coins themselves for reliance on BlackRock, its custodian and the market makers in between.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance to Close Accounts in Four EU Countries Dec. 31, Charging Idle Balances From Nov. 29
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance to Close Accounts in Four EU Countries Dec. 31, Charging Idle Balances From Nov. 29
Binance told users in France, Spain, Italy and Poland to withdraw their crypto, with deposits blocked, accounts closing Dec. 31 and a monthly fee starting Nov. 29, as the exchange still lack...
content:
Binance will close customer accounts in France, Spain, Italy and Poland on Dec. 31 and begin charging a monthly fee on leftover balances from Nov. 29, as the world’s largest crypto exchange still lacks a license under the European Union’s MiCA rules.

A Binance spokesperson confirmed to CoinDesk the closure date over the weekend, saying the exchange is “progressively restricting certain services for affected users” now that the transition period under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework has ended.

“Affected accounts will be closed with effect from 31 December 2026,” the spokesperson said, calling it “a carefully managed process.” Binance said customer assets remain safe and accessible and described the move as “no sudden freeze.”

Deposits are already blocked, but users can still withdraw crypto and fiat. Users in the four countries have shared the notices on X.

The fees and deadlines

According to emails that users shared, Binance will charge 0.025% of remaining crypto balances each month, or 10 USDC, whichever is higher, starting Nov. 29. The first charge lands within three days of that date, and a second follows after Dec. 24.

Fees come out of USDC first and then other assets. Accounts holding less than the fee would lose the entire balance, the emails say. Anyone who withdraws everything before Nov. 29 pays nothing.

Binance had not published those fee figures in a public announcement as of Sunday, so the details rest on the customer emails, not an official notice. The company’s spokesperson confirmed only the closure date and the restriction of services.

The four countries share one trait: Binance ran locally registered businesses in each before the MiCA transition ended. Its first outreach to users there came in June, when it urged them to withdraw.

A license Binance still has not won

MiCA requires crypto firms to win authorization in one EU member state before serving customers across the bloc. Binance withdrew its Greek license application in June and said it would seek approval elsewhere, without naming the country.

Reuters had reported that month that Greece’s Hellenic Capital Market Commission was poised to reject the bid, as Bitcoin Magazine reported. As the MiCA deadline arrived, the EU’s securities regulator also ordered unlicensed crypto firms to exit the market.

Binance told users at the time that it remained committed to Europe. It does not appear on the European Securities and Markets Authority’s register of authorized crypto providers, and it has not said which regulator now holds its application.

The closures arrive in a rough stretch for the exchange. Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Oct. 29 in a record heist the company said began with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job offers targeting engineers. Binance has said it will fully reimburse affected customers, and U.S. banking regulators have since quizzed banks following the hack.

On Saturday, Binance also said finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving after more than five years. Co-CEO Yi He said in a statement that the transition was planned over the last half year, and Justin Yek, most recently a finance vice president at Airwallex, takes over as CFO.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the theft, which Pyongyang has denied.

It is not clear how many Binance users are affected, and there is no sign so far that accounts in Germany or other EU countries are being closed. Notices cited by French media said accounts still holding assets after Dec. 31 would be treated as inactive.

Rivals that already hold MiCA licenses, including Coinbase and Kraken, stand to gain if Binance exits, as noted in June. The test for Binance is whether it can secure a license before more of its European business is wound down.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Ankr Bridge Exploit Sends $292K in Crypto to Attacker Through Five Fake Withdrawals
summary:
Key Takeaways: Blockaid reports that about $292,000 were stolen from Ankr’s Ethereum bridge through five suspicious withdrawals. The attacker is said to have used a small Optimism deposit to withdraw
The post Ankr Bridge Exploit Sends $292K in Crypto to Attacker Through Five Fake Withdrawals appeare...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Blockaid reports that about $292,000 were stolen from Ankr’s Ethereum bridge through five suspicious withdrawals.
  • The attacker is said to have used a small Optimism deposit to withdraw several assets.
  • Several Ankr operator wallets across three different networks were drained and merged into a single wallet days before the exploit.

Hackers exploited Ankr’s Ethereum Cross Chain bridge with five unauthorized withdrawals. Blockchain security firm Blockaid detected the activity on November 9, 2026, and warned that the attack was still ongoing when it published its alert.

🚨Blockaid detected an ongoing exploit on @ankr on Ethereum.
An attacker submitted five withdraw calls on Ankr’s Ethereum cross-chain bridge, using a tiny Optimism deposit to unlock the bridge’s full locked inventory to a new wallet.
~$292k drained from the bridge so far across ~5 txs. Attack still ongoing. 🧵

— Blockaid (@blockaid_) November 9, 2026

The incident points to the concern about how the bridge verifies the cross-chain transaction and grants asset releases.

  • One Optimism Deposit Linked to Five Withdrawals
  • Ankr Operator Wallets Were Swept Before the Attack
    • Five Transactions Targeted the Ethereum Bridge

One Optimism Deposit Linked to Five Withdrawals

Blockaid states that the attacker made 5 withdrawal calls on the Ankr’s Ethereum bridge. Those transactions reportedly involved depositing a small amount from Optimism to unlock assets from the Ethereum bridge contract.

The company estimated it lost about $292,000 in total in about five transactions. The money was moved to the withdrawing wallet in a new wallet address. It was not a single asset, it was multiple assets. These included Ankr-related liquid staking tokens and ANKR, Ankr’s native cryptocurrency.

Usually, a cross-chain bridge will unlock assets on a different chain following a deposit on the originating chain. If it has the same transaction as evidence of authorisation for another withdrawal, a single deposit might potentially be used more than once.

But Blockaid’s first alert failed to detail the exact technical flaw or how the attacker got past the authorization controls on the bridge.

Read More: Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After $2.7M Exploit Tied to Unauthorized Token Minting

Ankr Operator Wallets Were Swept Before the Attack

The on-chain activity that led up to the withdrawals also contributes to the occurrence. The Blockaid reported that between the time of 02:08 and 04:06 UTC, several Ankr operator wallets were emptied throughout Ethereum, Arbitrum and Linea. The money was deposited to a single consolidation wallet.

Next, the attacker transacted with this wallet to pay the fee for the relayer that submitted the transactions to the bridge.

It appears the attacks were executed after the attacker prepared the transaction infrastructure. But only the wallet moves don’t show how access to the operator wallets obtained and if their private keys breached.

Five Transactions Targeted the Ethereum Bridge

Blockaid found two exploit addresses and provided an example transaction with the exploited bridge contract.

All of the withdrawals were towards the same Ethereum Bridge, capital was sent to the attackers’ withdrawal wallet. The reported loss is for the money drained when Blockaid warned, not a final tally of the incident.

That’s significant because the attack continues to be active, even during the time of the alert sent by the security firm. The ultimate losses could be impacted by additional transactions and/or price adjustments for tokens.

The incident puts cross-chain verification under scrutiny. Bridges depend on reliable communication between networks, and their security relies on correctly validating deposits, messages, and withdrawal authorizations.

A failure in any part of that process can expose assets held in bridge contracts, even when the original deposit is legitimate.

title: Ondo Claims the Tokenisation Leadership on the Back of Securitize’s Shrinking Assets
summary:
Ondo Finance has overtaken Securitize to become the largest asset tokeniser by market value. In its November 5 announcement, Ondo reported more than $4 billion across 484 assets.
“Becoming the largest tokenisation platform in the world is a milestone for Ondo,” said Ian De Bode, its acting CEO and p...
content:
2026-11-09T17:06:00.000+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 15:06 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Ondo overtook Securitize after BUIDL’s outstanding supply fell by about $200 million, while Ondo’s total tokenised value remained broadly unchanged.
  • Both platforms remain concentrated in Treasury-linked products, with USDY representing almost 60% of Ondo’s value and BUIDL nearly half of Securitize’s.

Ondo Finance has overtaken Securitize to become the largest asset tokeniser by market value. In its November 5 announcement, Ondo reported more than $4 billion across 484 assets.

“Becoming the largest tokenisation platform in the world is a milestone for Ondo,” said Ian De Bode, its acting CEO and president.

But on-chain chronology tells a more cynical story: over the exact days Ondo claimed victory, its own platform assets barely budged, hovering flat at $4.04 billion.

Ondo Wins by Standing Still

On November 3, Ondo was already above $4 billion, trailing Securitize’s approximately $4.15 billion with $4.07 billion. Two days later, Ondo’s value was still around $4.07 billion, while Securitize had fallen to $3.97 billion.

By November 9, the gap had widened to roughly $226 million: Ondo held $4.04 billion against Securitize’s $3.81 billion in the ranking of tokenized asset value excluding stablecoins. The change came principally from the contraction on Securitize’s side.

A major contributor to the shift appeared to be BlackRock’s BUIDL. Its outstanding supply fell from approximately $2 billion on November 3 to $1.8 billion five days later, a decline larger than Securitize’s initial lead.

BUIDL - BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund - is managed by BlackRock Financial Management. However it uses Securitise’s tokenisation infrastructure and thus influences the platform’s total value.

Redemptions therefore reduce the assets attributed to Securitize even though it does not manage the underlying portfolio. BUIDL’s service arrangements explain how investor withdrawals from a BlackRock fund affect a technology provider’s ranking.

Capital Concentrated in One Product

According to RWA.xyz, Ondo’s product catalogue now counts 486 assets, which is nearly 10 times larger than 50 on Securitize. Still, both platforms have their own concentration issues.

Ondo’s yield-bearing token backed by short-term US Treasuries and bank deposits, accounts for approximately $2.39 billion, or 59% of its total. BUIDL represents about 47% of Securitize’s value.

RWA.xyz’s Treasury data therefore places substantial weight on one product at each platform. Concentration also extends to the investors behind those products.

OnChain Benchmark reported that Grove, a capital allocator in the Sky ecosystem, held 26.5% of BUIDL in August and had exited entirely by November 8. Its position accounted for roughly three-quarters of the fund’s net decline over that longer period.

Grove’s longer-term withdrawal illustrates the concentration behind the ranking, even though the available data does not identify who redeemed the final $200 million.

With USDY accounting for almost 60% of Ondo’s value and BUIDL for nearly half of Securitize’s, the leaderboard measures flows into a handful of Treasury-linked products more than demand across the hundreds of assets the platforms tokenise.

RWA.xyz’s Treasury data therefore places substantial weight on one product at each platform. Concentration also extends to the investors behind those products.

OnChain Benchmark reported that Grove, a capital allocator in the Sky ecosystem, held 26.5% of BUIDL in August and had exited entirely by November 8. Its position accounted for roughly three-quarters of the fund’s net decline over that longer period.

Grove’s longer-term withdrawal illustrates the concentration behind the ranking, even though the available data does not identify who redeemed the final $200 million.

With USDY accounting for almost 60% of Ondo’s value and BUIDL for nearly half of Securitize’s, the leaderboard measures flows into a handful of Treasury-linked products more than demand across the hundreds of assets the platforms tokenise.

title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
FinCEN and the Federal Reserve formally withdrew a 2020 proposal that would have cut the cross-border funds-transfer threshold from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, saying any future version ...
content:
FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place.

The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020.

That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more.

It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient.

Why the agencies backed off

Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels.

Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995.

Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it.

The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment.

The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.”

What the withdrawal does and does not do

The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule.

What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. The agencies did not say whether they plan a new proposal or offer a timeline.

The withdrawal is the latest in a run of reversals from Treasury. On Oct. 6, FinCEN scrapped its 2020 “unhosted wallet” proposal and a 2023 plan to label international crypto mixing a primary money laundering concern, a move Coin Center called a significant victory for financial privacy.

It does not signal a retreat from enforcement. On Friday, FinCEN cut off the MEXC exchange from the U.S. financial system over alleged sanctions evasion, using a different legal tool aimed at one named platform instead of a rule covering every institution.

Stablecoins are following their own track. Under the GENIUS Act, the Fed in June proposed customer identification requirements for stablecoin issuers, and FinCEN and the Treasury’s sanctions office proposed anti-money-laundering programs for the same firms in April.

For bitcoin users, the practical effect is that nothing changes: the $3,000 trigger stays, and the crypto-specific wording that industry groups opposed is gone for now.

Whether FinCEN and the Fed return with a new threshold, a crypto definition or neither will not be clear until one is published, and the agencies have committed to taking comments first.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto Firm Bullish Hires Former NYSE President Stacey Cunningham
summary:
Bullish named Stacey Cunningham, the former president of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), as its president, the crypto exchange operator said today (Monday). The hire reunites her with CEO Tom Farley, whom she succeeded at the NYSE in 2018.
Cunningham joins six months after Bullish, which listed ...
content:
2026-11-09T15:13:32.496+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 13:13 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • She takes the same title at a company run by Tom Farley, her predecessor at the New York exchange.
  • Its $4.2 billion deal for share-registry firm Equiniti still needs regulatory approval before a January close.

Bullish named Stacey Cunningham, the former president of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), as its president, the crypto exchange operator said today (Monday). The hire reunites her with CEO Tom Farley, whom she succeeded at the NYSE in 2018.

Cunningham joins six months after Bullish, which listed on the NYSE in August 2025 at $37 a share, agreed to pay $4.2 billion for Equiniti, a transfer agent serving nearly 3,000 companies that issue shares and more than 20 million shareholders.

Trading already earns Bullish less than its other businesses. Subscription, services and other revenue reached $62.7 million in the second quarter, against $29.9 million in adjusted transaction revenue.

Farley said she would help build new services for market participants and pointed to her decades of relationships with issuers, the customers Equiniti serves today.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Equiniti Is Working With Both Bullish and the NYSE

Public markets depend on trusted infrastructure, Cunningham said, and "there is an enormous opportunity to make that infrastructure more efficient, connected and accessible."

Bullish, the NYSE and Nasdaq have reached different stages with tokenized shares, digital versions of stock recorded on a blockchain .

The NYSE said in January it was building a round-the-clock tokenized venue that would need regulatory approval and has given no launch date, while Nasdaq, which asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in September 2025 to allow tokenized trading, won approval in March.

Bullish received approval from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission in June and began trading its own tokenized shares in August.

Equiniti appears on both sides. The NYSE named it on November 2 as one of six transfer agents signed up for the planned venue, and Cunningham still sits on the NYSE board, according to the Bullish release. The Equiniti purchase is expected to close in January, subject to regulatory approvals.

A Second Former NYSE President at Bullish

The two have worked together before. Cunningham reported to Farley as the NYSE's chief operating officer from 2015, then took over from him as president in May 2018.

"I've seen firsthand the impact of her leadership," Farley said in the statement.

She led the NYSE Group until January 2022, the first woman to do so, according to the company. Before the NYSE she held senior roles at Nasdaq.

She has worked as an operating partner at private equity firm Advent and an adviser to Uniswap Labs, and the company said she serves on the board of Cloudflare.

title: Nvidia Loses $225B in Market Value as Jensen Huang Faces Board Probe Over China Spy Allegations
summary: Nvidia shares fell more than 5% in premarket trading on November 9, wiping approximately $225 billion from the company’s market value after its board announced an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVDA

Nvidia shares fell more than 5% in premarket trading on November 9, wiping approximately $225 billion from the company’s market value after its board announced an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

The investigation follows reports linking Huang to Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, who US intelligence officials reportedly suspected of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. The controversy has raised questions about Nvidia’s corporate security, AI chip exports, and the potential national security implications of its international business relationships.

Nvidia Board Launches Independent Investigation Into Jensen Huang

Nvidia’s board announced the investigation on November 8 following reports that Huang may have been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, working with external legal counsel, will oversee the review.

Nvidia launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he disclosed an intimate relationship with a business executive later identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy. Source: The New York Times via X

In its official statement, the board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” However, it said the investigation would examine all available information and assess the circumstances surrounding the reported intelligence operation.

Huang has agreed to cooperate fully with the investigation. The board also expressed confidence in his leadership and indicated that further updates would be provided when appropriate.

The announcement followed reports that US authorities had examined Alice Huang’s connections to Nvidia and her relationship with its chief executive. The allegations have attracted attention because of Megaspeed’s role in purchasing advanced Nvidia processors amid Washington’s restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.

$4.8 Billion Nvidia Chip Purchases Raise Export Control Concerns

The investigation also places Megaspeed’s semiconductor purchases under greater scrutiny. According to reporting by The New York Times, the company’s Malaysian affiliate purchased at least $4.8 billion worth of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia technology between June 2024 and February 2026, based on trade records obtained from ImportGenius.

Nvidia’s Jensen Huang allegedly facilitated $4.8 billion in AI chip shipments to Chinese clients through Southeast Asia, bypassing U.S. export restrictions. Source: @tatthang via X

US authorities have examined whether Megaspeed helped Chinese companies obtain access to advanced AI processors restricted under American export controls. The company operates as a data center intermediary, purchasing computing equipment and renting processing capacity to customers, including Chinese technology group Alibaba.

The reported transactions have attracted attention because Washington has imposed restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports to limit China’s access to computing resources used in artificial intelligence development. Investigators reportedly suspect that some processors acquired through the Southeast Asian business network may have reached China in violation of those restrictions. However, the available reporting does not establish that every purchase or shipment breached US export rules. 

The allegations have also prompted separate scrutiny of Megaspeed’s operations. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs clarified on October 31 that its government had not investigated Alice Huang or expressed concerns about her alleged intelligence connections. However, Singapore’s police confirmed that investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing and declined to provide further details. 

Jensen Huang Admits Infidelity as China Spy Allegations Intensify

The controversy intensified after Huang sent an apology to Nvidia employees on November 8, acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Although he did not identify the woman involved, reports linked the relationship to Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia CEO.

In his message, Huang accepted responsibility for the personal and professional consequences of his actions. He apologized to his family, employees, board members, business partners, and shareholders, acknowledging that he had fallen short of the responsibility associated with leading the company.

China’s Foreign Ministry dismissed the allegations against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as unsubstantiated, calling them smears against China. Source: @clashreport via X

Huang also addressed the national security concerns directly, confirming his support for the board’s independent investigation and pledging full cooperation. He reaffirmed his commitment to Nvidia and said he would continue working to protect the company and support US national security. 

The allegations against Alice Huang remain a central part of the investigation. Reporting by The New York Times cited people briefed on classified intelligence who said US officials had concluded that she was gathering information for Beijing. The reporting also raised concerns about whether her access to Nvidia’s CEO could have exposed sensitive corporate or government-related information.

However, the intelligence allegations have not been established through a public investigation finding. China rejected the claims on November 9, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun describing them as unsubstantiated and an attempt to discredit Beijing. 

Nvidia Stock Faces Pressure Over Leadership Uncertainty

The investigation has added another source of uncertainty for Nvidia investors, who were already assessing concerns about the sustainability of AI-related spending. Nvidia shares had come under pressure alongside other technology stocks following a broader market downturn.

NVDA fell over 5% on November 9, wiping out approximately $225 billion in market value after news of a board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. Source: @KobeissiLetter via X

Early trading data on November 9 showed NVDA falling approximately 4.5% to 5% before the US market opened. Its market capitalization was estimated at around $4.51 trillion, representing an implied decline of roughly $225 billion from its previous valuation. The early movement highlighted how quickly concerns surrounding the company’s leadership can affect investor sentiment. 

The potential leadership implications are particularly relevant because Huang has led Nvidia for more than three decades and played a central role in its transformation into a dominant supplier of AI processors. His influence extends beyond product development, with the company’s global strategy and relationships across the technology industry closely associated with his leadership.

Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., warned that the investigation could create additional pressure on the stock. He said there was a risk Huang could be removed depending on the board’s findings, adding that the uncertainty would weigh on Nvidia because of the CEO’s importance to its global strategy. 

However, Nvidia has indicated that Huang intends to remain in his position while the review proceeds. A company spokesperson said he was committed to continuing as CEO without interruption. The board has also expressed confidence in his leadership team, although its investigation leaves questions about the potential consequences of the reported intelligence operation. 

The controversy also comes at a sensitive time for the semiconductor industry. US restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China remain a significant factor in Nvidia’s international business strategy. Greater scrutiny of its customers, distribution partners, and export compliance procedures could add regulatory pressure to an already complex market.

For now, the board’s investigation has not established that Nvidia’s trade secrets or US national security information were compromised. Its findings, together with the company’s response to export-control concerns, will be important in determining whether the controversy creates lasting consequences for Nvidia’s leadership, investor confidence, and position in the global AI market.

title: Bitrue AI Research Shows XRP Traded Higher 90 Days After 12 of 17 Oversold Readings
summary: San Jose, Costa Rica, 9th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

San Jose, Costa Rica, 9th November 2026, Chainwire

San Jose, Costa Rica, November 9th, 2026, Chainwire

New report combines a live read from Bitrue AI with every oversold XRP reading since 2023.

Bitrue Research Institute, the in-house research arm of cryptocurrency exchange Bitrue, has released Oversold XRP: The Road to Recovery and the Signals to Watch. Built on a live market read from Bitrue AI and daily XRP/USDT data from January 2023 onward, the study shows that XRP has historically built a base before recovering from oversold lows, and examines what has followed oversold conditions in XRP and which signals would show that buyers are returning.

XRP is trading 55.2% below its one-year high and is oversold on both the daily and 4-hour charts. Bitrue AI, Bitrue’s AI trading copilot, reads a 4-hour Relative Strength Index of 24 and flags the risk of a sharp rebound alongside the risk of continued decline. Its XRP strategy uses a working band of $1.0365 to $1.1803. Bitrue Research Institute independently recalculated these indicators and found consistent readings.

The study identifies 18 occasions since 2023 on which XRP’s daily RSI fell below 35. In 12 of the 17 cases with a full 90-day window, XRP traded higher 90 days later, compared with 53.5% of all days in the period. The report notes that the pattern was uneven across time horizons, that the sample is small, and that recoveries typically included a further dip before prices moved higher.

The report also finds that recoveries from XRP’s current market state have historically followed a base-building phase. Since 2023, conditions similar to today’s never moved directly into a confirmed uptrend. A trading range formed first in 43.9% of cases within 10 days, while a confirmed downtrend came first in 49.6%.

To help readers recognize when accumulation begins, the study sets out a checklist of confirmation signals. These include volume on up days overtaking volume on down days, on-balance volume turning positive while price holds, and a daily close above $1.1803, the top of Bitrue AI’s current band. Over the past 20 days, volume on down days has outweighed volume on up days by roughly two to one. The report stresses that these signals confirm accumulation as it happens rather than anticipate it. In August 2026, the shift in volume came on the day of a breakout, not before it.

Bitrue AI strategies, listed on the Bitrue AI strategy page, display their direction, price band and reasoning, and are refreshed every 15 minutes. Users set take-profit, stop-loss and maximum drawdown limits before a strategy starts.

“Oversold markets make traders ask whether the bottom is in,” said Bitrue Research Institute. “This report doesn’t answer that with a price target. It shows what has followed similar conditions and which signals would confirm that buyers are returning, and Bitrue AI is built to read those signals as they change and explain what it sees.”

The report describes historical frequencies and current conditions. It does not constitute a price forecast or investment advice, and past recoveries do not guarantee future ones.

About The Study

Oversold XRP: The Road to Recovery and the Signals to Watch uses daily and 4-hour XRP/USDT data from Bitrue’s public market data interface, cross-checked against an independent market data source. Indicators include RSI, the Average Directional Index, Bollinger Band width, on-balance volume and an up-day to down-day volume ratio. The full methodology is set out in the report.

The full report is available to download here.

About Bitrue Research Institute

Bitrue Research Institute is the in-house research arm of Bitrue. It studies digital asset markets using Bitrue’s own market data alongside public market and on-chain sources, with a focus on XRP, market structure and the role of AI in trading. The institute publishes regular market commentary and data-driven reports, and its analysis has been cited by international financial and crypto media. It works closely with the Bitrue AI team, applying the platform’s AI tools in its own research and examining how automated strategies behave across different market conditions.

About Bitrue

Founded in 2018, Bitrue is a trusted global cryptocurrency exchange with over eight years of industry experience, serving more than 40 million users worldwide. Bitrue was the first exchange to list XRP as a base pair and continues to offer one of the broadest selections of XRP trading pairs available on any global exchange, alongside a growing suite of tokenized real-world assets, staking products, Launchpool offerings, and Bitrue AI, its free AI-powered trading bot, visit bitrue.com.

About Bitrue AI

Bitrue AI is Bitrue’s beginner-friendly AI trading copilot, built to make AI trading as simple as possible through real-time AI strategies, continuous market adaptation, and Explainable AI that shows traders not just what to do, but why.

content:
2026-11-09T13:02:08.430+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 11:02 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • cTrader connects broker data to ChatGPT, Claude and other compatible AI applications.
  • Brokers can use AI to review trading activity, margin levels and financial records.

Spotware has introduced an AI integration for cTrader Admin, allowing brokers to connect compatible AI applications to platform data and investigate trading activity through natural-language requests.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The move follows the launch of cTrader AI Agent Connect in May 2026, which allowed traders to connect AI applications to their accounts through MCP servers. The new release extends this connectivity to broker operations.

AI Tools Investigate Rejected Orders and Executions

Included in cTrader Admin version 10.4, the MCP server supports applications such as ChatGPT Desktop, Claude and Codex CLI. Managers can use it to investigate trading incidents, review exposure, compare account performance and inspect platform settings.

For client complaints about rejected orders, the assistant retrieves order histories and linked deals. It checks them against account permissions, symbol settings and trading conditions to reconstruct events.

For disputed execution prices, it compares deal records with order timelines, pricing settings and historical market data. If the evidence does not establish a cause, it identifies remaining uncertainties and further checks required.

cTrader Adds AI-Powered Broker Risk Reviews

Managers can also review exposure across client accounts. They can examine bought, sold and net volumes by symbol, currency and book, with A-book and B-book positions shown separately. The system can identify accounts with the largest unrealised gains and losses and those closest to stop-out by comparing equity and margin levels with group settings.

Other functions include reviewing realised trading results, investigating position charges and checking balance movements. It can compare symbol specifications, trading sessions, limits and markups against broker requirements, as well as examine historical price data for gaps and unusual activity.

Irina Olyaeva, Product Manager for cTrader Admin at Spotware, said the integration aims to “reduce the time managers spend collecting records during investigations” while keeping access and operational decisions under the broker's control.

The server runs locally within cTrader Admin and requires an authenticated manager session. Access follows existing permissions. All operations are read-only, so the assistant cannot execute trades or change account settings or platform configurations. Managers must verify its findings before making operational decisions.

title: Finance Magnates Announces the CEO of the Year (B2B) 2026
summary:
Finance Magnates has named Cristian Vlasceanu, CEO of Centroid Solutions, as Fintech (B2B) CEO of the Year 2026, recognising his leadership in expanding the company's trading technology and financial infrastructure offering through the development of the One-Centroid Ecosystem.
The award was announc...
content:
2026-11-09T12:37:51.702+02:00

Monday, 09/11/2026 | 10:37 GMT by FM

Disclaimer

  • Cristian Vlasceanu, CEO of Centroid Solutions, has been named Fintech (B2B) CEO of the Year 2026 at the Finance Magnates Awards.
  • His recognition highlights the role of integrated technology in supporting brokers, fintech providers and financial institutions.

Finance Magnates has named Cristian Vlasceanu, CEO of Centroid Solutions, as Fintech (B2B) CEO of the Year 2026, recognising his leadership in expanding the company's trading technology and financial infrastructure offering through the development of the One-Centroid Ecosystem.

The award was announced at the Finance Magnates Awards Gala Dinner & Ceremony in Limassol, Cyprus, on 6 November 2026, recognising business leaders and companies across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services.

Vlasceanu's recognition reflects Centroid's expansion from its established brokerage connectivity and risk management solutions into a broader technology offering covering multi-asset trading, client lifecycle management and embedded finance infrastructure.

Cristian Vlasceanu: From Software Engineering to CEO

Recognized as an authority on cutting-edge technology, Cristian Vlasceanu rose through software engineering roles to lead Centroid Solutions as CEO.

He oversees a talented team, supports clients, and drives product improvement. Guided by a forward-looking vision, Cristian led Centroid to establish its One-Centroid Ecosystem, broadening the offering to include a multi-asset trading platform and CLM/CRM alongside its core connectivity bridge, risk engine, and network infrastructure solutions.

Expanding Centroid's Trading Technology Ecosystem

Under Vlasceanu's leadership, Centroid has brought together several technology solutions supporting different aspects of brokerage and financial operations:

  • CS 360: Liquidity connectivity, aggregation and order management.

  • C2C: A multi-asset trading and investing platform.

  • C 24: Risk management and trading exposure monitoring.

  • CS Maystro: Client lifecycle management, onboarding and CRM.

  • CS Drive: Hosting and network infrastructure for financial institutions.

Together, these products form the One-Centroid Ecosystem, which Centroid positions as a modular technology offering for brokers, banks and fintech businesses. The integrated approach also supports embedded finance by connecting trading and investment services with broader financial applications.

Supporting Technology Development in B2B Financial Services

For brokers and institutional market participants, the integration of trading technology with operational systems can affect how efficiently they manage liquidity, monitor exposure, onboard clients and introduce new services.

Centroid's approach addresses these requirements through an architecture designed to reduce reliance on disconnected technology components while supporting different business models.

Alongside the CEO recognition, Centroid Solutions was named Best Bridge Provider 2026 in the Finance Magnates Awards' Tech for Brokers category, recognising its work in trading connectivity technology.

Finance Magnates Awards 2026: Recognising B2B Leadership

The Finance Magnates Awards 2026 recognised two CEOs in separate categories, highlighting leadership across both financial technology and brokerage services.

While Cristian Vlasceanu received the Fintech (B2B) CEO of the Year award, Ziad Melhem of CFI Financial Group was named Brokerage (B2C) CEO of the Year 2026.

For the complete results, read the Finance Magnates Awards 2026 winners announcement.

  • Ziad Melhem, Group CEO of CFI Financial Group, has been named Brokerage (B2C) CEO of the Year 2026 at the Finance Magnates Awards.
  • The recognition highlights Melhem's focus on governance, technology, operational performance and long-term growth in online brokerage services.

Finance Magnates has named Ziad Melhem, Group CEO of CFI Financial Group, as Brokerage (B2C) CEO of the Year 2026, recognising his contribution to the company's record trading performance and continued development as an international brokerage group.

The award was announced at the Finance Magnates Awards Gala Dinner & Ceremony in Limassol, Cyprus, on 6 November 2026, recognising business leaders and companies across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services.

Since becoming Group CEO in June 2025, Melhem has overseen a period of increased client activity, business development and investment in CFI's long-term capabilities.

Ziad Melhem: From Group CMO to CEO

Ziad Melhem is CEO of CFI Financial Group, leading the Group’s global strategy, operational performance and expansion across MENA and key international markets. Previously CFI’s Group CMO, he brings extensive experience across finance, technology and business development, with a focus on long-term value creation, client trust and sustainable growth.

Melhem's involvement with CFI began in 2022, when he served as a board advisor. He subsequently joined the company's executive leadership team before being appointed Group CEO in June 2025.

CFI Reports Record Trading Volumes Under Melhem's Leadership

CFI Financial Group reported its strongest first half on record in 2026, supported by increased trading activity and client engagement.

According to the company's July 2026 performance announcement:

  • Q2 trading volume: $3.03 trillion, an increase of 101% year-on-year.

  • H1 trading volume: $5.34 trillion, marking a record first half.

  • Active clients: Increased by 8.4% year-on-year.

  • Trade executions: More than 42.47 million trades in Q2 2026, up 74% year-on-year.

The results reflect growing activity across CFI's trading platforms, with metals and equity indices contributing to client trading volumes.

Expanding CFI's Global Brokerage Operations

Alongside its trading performance, CFI has continued expanding into international markets, with an emphasis on establishing locally regulated operations and broadening its financial services.

In April 2026, CFI announced that it had secured authorisation from the Central Bank of Brazil to operate as a securities brokerage firm, supporting its expansion into Latin America following its launch in Colombia.

The Group also expanded its product offering, introducing local stock trading in the UAE and broadening its services in Bahrain to include regulated digital asset products following regulatory approval.

Technology investment has accompanied this expansion, including the development of CFI's Global Technology Center in Malaysia, which supports engineering, product development and the Group's international trading operations.

Together, these initiatives reflect Melhem's stated objective of building CFI into a global financial services institution with stronger operational and regulatory foundations.

Finance Magnates Awards 2026: Recognising B2C Leadership

The Finance Magnates Awards 2026 recognised two CEOs in separate categories, highlighting leadership across brokerage services and financial technology.

While Ziad Melhem received the Brokerage (B2C) CEO of the Year award, Cristian Vlasceanu of Centroid Solutions was named Fintech (B2B) CEO of the Year 2026.

Alongside Melhem's individual recognition, CFI Financial Group received two additional awards: Most Established Broker 2026 (MENA) and Most Innovative Broker 2026 (UAE).

The B2C CEO recognition reflects the role of executive leadership in balancing commercial performance, client needs and the operational requirements of running a brokerage across multiple markets.

For the complete results, read the Finance Magnates Awards 2026 winners announcement.

title: Morgan Stanley Tokenizes U.S. Stocks and Treasuries on DTCC’s $114T Asset Platform
summary:
Key Takeaways: Morgan Stanley is one of the first banks adopting DTCC’s new tokenization service. The bank is participating in tokenizing the U.S. equity and Treasury securities holdings at DTC.
The post Morgan Stanley Tokenizes U.S. Stocks and Treasuries on DTCC’s $114T Asset Platform appeared firs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Morgan Stanley is one of the first banks adopting DTCC’s new tokenization service.
  • The bank is participating in tokenizing the U.S. equity and Treasury securities holdings at DTC.
  • According to DTCC, the service creates opportunities for increased asset mobility, liquidity and capital efficiency.

DTCC’s new Tokenization Service, known as DTS, is another step in the venture of real-world asset tokenization by Morgan Stanley. The Wall Street bank indicated it’s one of the first financial institutions to tokenize U.S. equities and Treasuries on the platform.

We are thrilled to announce that Morgan Stanley is among the first banks to tokenize real-world assets following the launch of the @The_DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS), converting U.S. Equity and U.S. Treasuries to tokenized form.

Launched on October 28, DTS creates tokenized representations of DTC-custodied securities to support greater liquidity, collateral mobility and capital efficiency.

— Morgan Stanley (@MorganStanley) November 3, 2026

  • Morgan Stanley Moves U.S. Securities Onchain
  • Tokenized Assets Keep Their Traditional Rights
    • DTCC Targets Faster Collateral Movement
    • $114T Custody Giant Expands Into Tokenization

Morgan Stanley Moves U.S. Securities Onchain

DTCC officially introduced DTS on October 28, which is a new tokenized offering of traditional securities and enters into a regulated market infrastructure.

Eligible DTC participants can issue digital securities on the service that are backed by securities they already hold at the DTC. Those assets are also transferrable from traditional storage to blockchain storage and hold the same ownership rights and economic value.

Twenty DTCs have signed deals to allow users to access the service, including Morgan Stanley. Other companies involved are JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, Barclays, Fidelity Investments, State Street and UBS.

Read More: Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing

Tokenized Assets Keep Their Traditional Rights

According to DTCC, the tokenized securities are digital replicas of assets held by DTC. This is because investors would not receive a synthesised product. The token is issued as a representation of an entitlement related to the underlying security and aims to maintain investor protections and economic rights.

Eligible assets may be switched from their traditional to tokenized state, providing institutions with the ability to leverage regulated securities in blockchain-based processes.

DTCC Targets Faster Collateral Movement

Key objectives of DTS include making securities more mobile and easier to deploy. According to DTCC, tokenization will enable institutions to tap into new liquidity pools, move collateral across faster, and balance capital utilization. It provides service for handling token transferring between 24/7 registered digital wallets that are compatible with approved digital networks.

DTS initially launched with the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network. DTCC is looking to expand its networks in 2027. The platform features a limited number of highly liquid securities, such as selected Russell 1,000 stocks, large-cap index ETFs and U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds.

$114T Custody Giant Expands Into Tokenization

DTCC’s launch is noteworthy for the entire tokenized real-world asset market, due to the size of their infrastructure.

To date, DTC has over $114 trillion in securities assets held, providing a significant pool that may be integrated into tokenized workflows over time.

DTCC previously conducted a test in July, and about 40 companies took part in live production trades of tokenized U.S. Treasuries and stocks. The transactions encompassed transactions that took place under the Treasury Repo regime as well as buy-sell trades and equity delivery-versus-payment transactions.

By joining, Morgan Stanley brings the technology from the testing phase into the active usage of the technology by institutions via a live tokenization platform.

title: South Korea Tightens Crypto Exchange Defenses After Binance’s $6.3B Security Breach
summary:
Key Takeaways: South Korea announced that it will examine local crypto exchanges following a $6.3 billion hack at Binance. The exchanges should increase their holdings in cold wallets and improve
The post South Korea Tightens Crypto Exchange Defenses After Binance’s $6.3B Security Breach appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • South Korea announced that it will examine local crypto exchanges following a $6.3 billion hack at Binance.
  • The exchanges should increase their holdings in cold wallets and improve withdrawal rules, regulators said.
  • Platforms were told to boost monitoring, incident response and reserve buffers.

South Korea is stepping up measures to make crypto exchanges safer in the wake of the Binance hack, which resulted in the loss of more than $6.3 billion from the world’s leading digital asset exchange.

The country’s big financial regulator has embarked on an emergency examination of domestic exchanges, including the systems for controlling access to wallets.

  • South Korea Scrutinizes Crypto Exchange Wallet Security
  • Binance Hack Puts Hot-Wallet Risks Back in Focus
    • Exchanges Told to Monitor Crypto Flows Around the Clock
    • Crypto Security Controls Move Beyond Cold Wallet Ratios

South Korea Scrutinizes Crypto Exchange Wallet Security

The Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting on Nov. 2 with the Financial Supervisory Service, Financial Security Institute, Digital Asset eXchange Alliance and major virtual asset service providers.

The review was centered on the user access to exchanges IT systems and administrator privileges granted to their customers, as well as crypto withdrawals approval and signing from hot wallets.

The regulator directed the platforms to boost the proportion of customer money in cold chains where private keys are not stored online and are less vulnerable to going through remote attacks. Local news reports state that South Korea has already mandated 80% of virtual asset assignees’ customers’ crypto assets be kept in cold wallets.

Binance Hack Puts Hot-Wallet Risks Back in Focus

Binance reported on Oct. 30 that it had seen unapproved withdrawals of about $6.3 billion from Binance’s hot wallets, the FSC said.

Potential attack vectors are being considered, such as vulnerability of employee work computers and access to internal systems or unauthorised contact with the transaction approval or signing systems. The regulator did not present those scenarios as confirmed findings.

Binance has stated that they will compensate their customers with the company’s funds or other reserves. Since then, the exchange has also started to monitor and freeze stolen assets.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

Exchanges Told to Monitor Crypto Flows Around the Clock

Cold storage is just one action that the FSC encourages. The agency also advised exchanges to keep a close watch on deposits and withdrawals, deploy staff dedicated to incident response and issue alerts in a timely manner to unusual access attempts to facilitate industry-wide sharing of information.

Platforms also were advised to make further investments in reserves which could offset any losses incurred in future security threats.

The steps are taken as Binance is grappling with the financial losses from the hack. Binance reported net $4.72B withdrawn in a resumption of withdrawals, though they noted outflows were beginning to ease.

Crypto Security Controls Move Beyond Cold Wallet Ratios

The Binance attack had made a point of how a company’s more assets it stores offline do not somehow single-handedly reduce risks related to privileged accounts, its devices, or systems for signing transactions.

That explains why South Korea’s review is targeting both asset custody and operational controls.

If another attack happens, the FSC will continue its efforts with regulators and crypto businesses to prevent further intrusions and mitigate losses, it said.

title: Hyperliquid Whale Shorts $5.44M in NVDA at 10x After Jensen Huang Affair Admission
summary:
Key Takeaways: A Hyperliquid whale shorted 30,000 contracts of NVDA, which is approximately $5.44 million. Upon NVIDIA Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang making public admission that he was unfaithful to
The post Hyperliquid Whale Shorts $5.44M in NVDA at 10x After Jensen Huang Affair Admission ap...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • A Hyperliquid whale shorted 30,000 contracts of NVDA, which is approximately $5.44 million.
  • Upon NVIDIA Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang making public admission that he was unfaithful to his wife, the trade came along.
  • The role will emphasize how equity news impacts the cryptocurrency perpetual markets when the equity markets are closed.

A crypto trader with a large stake has created a big bearish position on NVIDIA using Hyperliquid, a 24/7 crypto perpetual futures marketplace, to trade exposure to NVIDIA out of regular US market hours.

Shortly after Huang’s public admission, Blockchain analytics account Lookonchain noted the same position stating that the trade has been done from Hyperliquid’s wallet visible on Hypurrscan.

  • Whale Takes $5.44M NVDA Short With 10x Leverage
  • Crypto Perpetuals Give Traders a Weekend NVDA Market
    • NVDA Perpetuals React Before Wall Street Reopens

Whale Takes $5.44M NVDA Short With 10x Leverage

The wallet had shorted 30,000 perpetual NVDA contracts and had a notional exposure of approximately $5.44 million with a 10x leverage.

Trade data available indicated that the price entered near $181.33 per contract, which takes the overall trade position size close to the total that is reported by Lookonchain.

After Jensen Huang admitted having an affair, a whale opened a 10x short on 30,000 $NVDA ($5.44M) on Hyperliquid.

https://t.co/RztJx5FNge https://t.co/zuyV2K0ftN

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 9, 2026

Relatively small price changes can result in substantial percentage changes for the trader’s collateral with a 10x leverage rate. A declining NVDA price will work in the favor of shorts, but a big rally can have a negative impact on those who are looking to liquidate.

The job does not suggest that the trader was wagering the bet specifically with respect to Huang’s disclosure. Public blockchain data indicates when and how the position was opened, but doesn’t reveal the wallet owner’s motivation or that a trade is a hedging move in another position.

Read More: Tornado Cash-Linked Wallet Sells ETH to Buy Zcash on Hyperliquid

Crypto Perpetuals Give Traders a Weekend NVDA Market

The timing may be significant as well because Hyperliquid work’s on Saturdays and Sundays.

Unlike regular NVIDIA, Nasdaq perpetual contracts do not close on weekends but give crypto investors directional exposure without the actual purchase of the shares.

It created a forum for traders to respond swiftly upon hearing NVIDIA’s announcement of Huang’s action and board’s independent inquiry. NVIDIA’s review is of reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency, the board said it did not believe at present that company secrets or national security were compromised.

NVDA Perpetuals React Before Wall Street Reopens

The leverage short coincided with a downtrend in NVIDIA-related markets. Traders digested the weekend developments as NVIDIA near $180.30, about 3.4% off Friday’s $186.64 closing price on the Nasdaq, per Reuters reports.

It gives another application of perpetual exchanges to the crypto markets: trading around the clock tokenized or synthetic exposure to traditional assets.

The $5.44 million whale trade isn’t as much about predicting potential NVIDIA price moves as it is about how fast the leveraged crypto markets can nail down big corporate news before the market closes at regular time.
