title: North Korea Rejects $6.3B Binance Crypto Heist Claims, FBI Blames TraderTraitor
summary:
Key Takeaways: North Korea has denied that state-sponsored cyber criminals raided about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrencies from Binance. The FBI reports that the attack was executed by a North Korea
The post North Korea Rejects $6.3B Binance Crypto Heist Claims, FBI Blames TraderTraitor appeared first...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • North Korea has denied that state-sponsored cyber criminals raided about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrencies from Binance.
  • The FBI reports that the attack was executed by a North Korea cyber unit known as TraderTraitor, which it estimates is moving large volumes of cryptocurrency after the attack into Ether.
  • Binance states that it has already reimbursed nearly 95% of the sum up to now, and that withdrawals have restarted in stages.

After the FBI formally accused a state-sponsored hacking campaign called TraderTraitor, North Korea issued denials for the record-breaking attack on Binance.

The dispute comes as investigators track billions of dollars in stolen crypto moving across blockchains, DeFi protocols and swap services.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • North Korea Rejects FBI Attribution for Binance Hack
  • Stolen Crypto Is Being Shifted Into Ethereum
    • Binance Covers Losses as Billions Leave the Exchange
    • Crypto Investigators Focus on the Laundering Trail

North Korea Rejects FBI Attribution for Binance Hack

Kim Yo Jong, a senior North Korean official and sister of leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the US allegation as politically motivated and described the FBI’s claim as “absurd rhetoric,” according to state media.

They had been involved in stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance around October 29 according to the FBI. Binance also pegged the estimated loss at approximately $6.3 billion on its own.

The operation, formerly known as TraderTraitor, could be related to North Korea’s crypto-related hacking efforts, U.S. investigators have concluded.

Stolen Crypto Is Being Shifted Into Ethereum

The FBI stated that it has seen these attackers turning the stolen assets into Ether, with more anticipated to be rendered through DeFi venues and instant-swap platforms.

Authorities have requested the crypto exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other participants in this industry to freeze transactions from these wallets of dubious origin.

The size of the theft made it one of the largest ever in the crypto security area. The USDC value of 1.1 billion or more as of Nov. 2 is frozen, whereas $3.28 billion worth of Bitcoin and Ether are still in the hands of hackers, Reuters reported.

Binance Covers Losses as Billions Leave the Exchange

There were also significant withdrawals that were made from Binance due to the hack. After reopening withdrawals, customers withdrew a net $4.72 billion, with approximately $2.7B returns flowing back after the opening. The withdrawals accounted for about 3% of all assets on the platform, said Binance, and outflows were starting to level off.

Binance has stated numerous times that users will not bear any financial burden. According to the exchange, by November 2, it had received about 95% of the amount. It’s resting on the latest Proof of Reserves update where the percentages of the tokens backed were 1:1 for ETC, USDT, BTC, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1 and ZEC.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B 

Crypto Investigators Focus on the Laundering Trail

The main issue now is how much of the remaining crypto could be ‘frozen’ to be dispersed among more wallets, chains, and liquidity markets.

The clearness that blockchain transactions provide, enables investigators to follow a trail. The challenge is speed because after being moved through cross-chain infrastructure, decentralized exchanges and instant swaps, it can be difficult to recover the stolen assets.

The FBI said it expects TraderTraitor to continue attempting to obscure the origin of the stolen funds as the laundering process develops.

title: Crypto News Today: Saylor Hints at Bitcoin Buy as Buterin Questions Ethereum Burn Thesis, and Schwartz Downplays XRP Price Influence
summary: Three prominent crypto figures have drawn attention to separate market issues as fresh Bitcoin buying speculation, an Ethereum tokenomics debate, and XRP price criticism converge.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Three prominent crypto figures have drawn attention to separate market issues as fresh Bitcoin buying speculation, an Ethereum tokenomics debate, and XRP price criticism converge.

Michael Saylor has revived expectations of another Bitcoin acquisition by Strategy after sharing its long-term accumulation chart. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin, meanwhile, has challenged the investment argument built around ETH’s fee-burning mechanism. At Ripple, former chief technology officer David Schwartz has responded to criticism over XRP’s declining price, describing his personal influence as very limited.

Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin Chart Fuels New Purchase Speculation

Michael Saylor renewed speculation about Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation plans on November 8 after posting a chart from SaylorTracker.com. Captioned “Connecting the dots,” the visualization showed the company’s Bitcoin treasury valued at approximately $64.44 billion, with 849,327 BTC held across 120 purchase events.

The visualization tracks 120 Bitcoin purchases against historical price movements, highlighting the company’s consistent accumulation strategy across market cycles. Source: Michael Saylor via X

The chart traced Strategy’s acquisition history against Bitcoin’s price movements, illustrating how the company continued accumulating the cryptocurrency through different market conditions. It listed an average acquisition cost of approximately $75,446 per BTC, highlighting the scale of the company’s long-term treasury strategy.

Although Saylor’s post attracted attention from investors anticipating another purchase, it did not confirm a new transaction. He has frequently shared similar accumulation updates before Strategy releases its weekly Bitcoin acquisition disclosures. The latest message therefore raised expectations rather than establishing that another purchase had taken place.

The post followed Strategy’s November 2 announcement that it had acquired 811 BTC for approximately $65.5 million between October 26 and November 1. According to the company’s SEC filing, the purchase brought total holdings to 849,327 BTC, acquired for an aggregate $64.08 billion at an average cost of $75,451 per coin.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Strategy also repurchased approximately $208.2 million worth of its STRC preferred shares during the same reporting period. The company used its existing dollar-denominated cash for the repurchase, while proceeds from selling 1,178,552 MSTR common shares helped finance the Bitcoin acquisition. The share sales generated approximately $164 million, of which $65.5 million funded the purchase and the remaining $98.5 million went toward its cash balance.

Saylor’s activity around STRC has also drawn attention to Strategy’s broader financing structure. The preferred security, traded on Nasdaq under the ticker STRC, forms part of the company’s digital credit strategy. Saylor discussed the financial foundations of the product in a separate November 7 post, writing that “Digital credit took four centuries to make possible.”

Investors will now look to Strategy’s next official disclosure for confirmation of any additional Bitcoin purchases. Until the company reports another transaction, Saylor’s latest chart remains an indication of its established accumulation approach rather than proof of a new acquisition.

Vitalik Buterin Questions Ethereum’s Fee-Burning Valuation Model

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has challenged the idea that ETH’s long-term market value should depend primarily on transaction-fee burning. He believes positioning the asset as a store of value offers a more dependable investment narrative than treating token destruction as the primary source of its economic worth.

Vitalik Buterin favors ETH as a store of value over a fee-burning token, citing Ethereum’s core principles of decentralization, privacy, and security. Source: @VitalikButerin via X

The debate centers on EIP-1559, Ethereum’s 2021 upgrade that introduced a mechanism for permanently removing the base portion of transaction fees from circulation. When the amount of ETH burned exceeds the issuance paid to validators, the network’s total supply can decline. This mechanism helped establish the “ultrasound money” narrative among investors during the previous bull market.

Buterin questioned whether the mechanism provides a reliable valuation floor. He illustrated the traditional argument with a hypothetical network generating $1 billion in annual token burns. Applying a 4% discount rate would produce an estimated valuation of $25 billion under that model.

However, Buterin argued that this calculation assumes the underlying revenue remains dependable. Ethereum’s historical fee generation has been heavily influenced by activity within the cryptocurrency market itself. Speculative trading, NFT launches, and other periods of intense on-chain demand have produced unusually high transaction costs, but those conditions can fade when market sentiment weakens.

The Otherside NFT land sale in 2022 provided one example of this volatility. The event generated an exceptional spike in Ethereum transaction fees, demonstrating how a single speculative episode could temporarily increase token burning. Buterin argued that such activity does not necessarily provide the stable external revenue required to establish a lasting valuation floor.

He also maintained that Ethereum should not abandon EIP-1559. Instead, he suggested that investors should not be concerned if fee burning remains below the level needed to offset new ETH issuance. As he explained, “the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.”

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Buterin identified decentralization, censorship resistance, open-source development, privacy, and security as more important foundations for Ethereum’s long-term appeal. He also warned that attempting to maximize transaction-fee revenue could push the network toward higher gas prices, extensive protocol spending, and more interventionist governance.

Such changes could undermine the characteristics that distinguish Ethereum from traditional financial infrastructure. Higher transaction costs could also make the network less accessible to users who depend on privacy and security.

His store-of-value argument also considers the network’s potential role in supporting tokenized real-world assets. Greater adoption of assets issued directly on Ethereum’s base layer could give ETH additional utility as collateral while strengthening its position within the financial ecosystem. Buterin further emphasized long-term network survival, including security improvements and preparation for post-quantum cryptography.

The comments represent a change in emphasis rather than a proposal to remove Ethereum’s existing fee-burning mechanism. Buterin’s broader argument is that ETH should derive its investment appeal from the durability and reliability of its underlying infrastructure, rather than depending on unpredictable periods of elevated transaction activity.

David Schwartz Downplays His Influence Over XRP Price

Ripple’s former chief technology officer David Schwartz has addressed renewed criticism from XRP holders following the token’s prolonged decline. His response came after cryptocurrency commentator Digital Asset Investor highlighted an exchange involving Schwartz on X, where investors questioned whether he had any responsibility for XRP’s market performance.

Schwartz says his influence over XRP’s price is minimal despite accusations of responsibility.  Source: @JoelKatz via X

One user challenged Schwartz to acknowledge his connection to the token’s price, arguing that holders’ frustration was not without reason. Schwartz responded candidly when asked whether he could honestly claim to have no influence over XRP.

“Can I honestly say that I have nothing to do with the price of XRP? I guess probably not nothing. But very little,” he replied.

The statement acknowledged that his actions and public comments may have some influence, while rejecting the idea that he has substantial control over XRP’s market valuation. The exchange did not identify any specific decision by Schwartz that caused the cryptocurrency’s decline.

The discussion unfolded as XRP traded near $1.16 on November 8. The token had lost approximately 49.78% over the preceding year, leaving it considerably below its July 2025 all-time high of $3.65. Its performance has increased frustration among some holders who expected stronger price gains despite continued developments across the XRP Ledger ecosystem.

Charts shared during the discussion also compared XRP’s 2026 performance with declines in Stellar (XLM) and Solana (SOL). The comparison highlighted broader weakness across several digital assets, although similar price movements do not establish that the tokens experienced identical market pressures.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Schwartz has also addressed the growing number of cryptocurrency-related messages appearing beneath his posts about unrelated subjects. He said some accounts had used those conversations to accuse him of fraud, criticize Ripple, or promote XRP. According to his explanation, he began blocking accounts that repeatedly disrupted discussions, regardless of whether their messages supported or criticized him.

His response came amid broader questions about the relationship between Ripple’s technical progress, XRP Ledger adoption, and the token’s market performance. However, developments in network infrastructure do not automatically translate into immediate price appreciation. XRP continues to trade in an open market where investor demand, liquidity, wider cryptocurrency trends, and market sentiment influence its valuation.

Schwartz’s comments therefore offer a distinction between his individual influence and the broader forces governing XRP’s price. While he acknowledged that his involvement is not entirely without effect, he made clear that his ability to determine the token’s market performance is limited.

title: Binance CFO Kaiser Ng Exits After 5 Years, Justin Yek Takes Over Finance Leadership
summary:
Key Takeaways: After five years, CFO of Binance, Kaiser Ng stepped down to head other businesses. He will be replaced by Airwallex vice president of finance, Justin Yek. Ng will
The post Binance CFO Kaiser Ng Exits After 5 Years, Justin Yek Takes Over Finance Leadership appeared first on CryptoNinja...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • After five years, CFO of Binance, Kaiser Ng stepped down to head other businesses.
  • He will be replaced by Airwallex vice president of finance, Justin Yek.
  • Ng will pursue the opportunities in AI, Web3 tokenization, sports, entertainment and robotics.

Following the decision of its chief financial officer, Kaiser Ng, to resign, Binance is looking to replace him. Ng shared his recollections of the exchange business and announced his intentions to establish businesses based on new technologies and blockchain own assets.

  • Kaiser Ng Reflects on Five Years at Binance
  • Justin Yek Named as His Successor
    • Ng Plans New Ventures in AI and Web3

Kaiser Ng Reflects on Five Years at Binance

Ng announced his departure in a post on X, saying he had decided to pursue several projects of his own. He described his time at Binance as one of the most rewarding periods of his career, despite the challenges facing the crypto industry.

After five years as CFO of Binance, I have decided to go build something of my own.

The past ten years in the digital asset exchange space have felt surprisingly short, because I enjoyed what I was doing. Having passion for what you do is so important, and I will come back to this point. 8am to 2am became a work habit. When I felt exhausted past midnight, I would just look up at the Kobe Bryant’s statue standing in the corner of my office, and go right back to the grind!

It has been the privilege of my career to help steward the finances of the world’s largest digital asset exchange through a period that tested our industry in every way: bull and bear cycles, Operation Choke Point 2.0, and a regulatory landscape that evolved as quickly as the technology itself. Finance is seldom the loudest function in a company, but it is where trust is earned. Over these five years, we transformed Finance from a pure back-office function into one that consistently generates new ideas and revenue opportunities for the company. We became amazing problem solvers. Finance understood the products and metrics as well as the business units themselves. Proud of what we have built together, and I am pleased to hand the keys to Justin, our next CFO.

I want to take this opportunity to thank CZ, Yi, Richard, and the leadership team for their confidence and, above all, the amazing Binancians around the world whom I had the honor of working with. You are the reason the company stands where it does today. Binance is in very capable hands.

The company continues to grow and evolve with the successful launch of TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces. I’d like to express my gratitude to MGX for the trust; to our home regulator Abu Dhabi Global Market and all regulators we work closely with; and to our business partners, including BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, our banking partners and payment channels, as well as our advisors and auditors. Special thanks to Grant Thornton Singapore and everyone who has supported Binance.

As for what comes next, well, there isn’t just one project but several that I am passionate about particularly in sports and entertainment, from basketball and music, to GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles. Bringing these real-world assets onto the blockchain through tokenization is a massive opportunity for the industry, and a big unlock for everyone. I welcome anyone with a passion in these areas to message me and potentially join my team. Even better if you love Kobe ;)

Moving from the CFO’s chair to the founder’s is a leap, and I take it with humility. I deeply believe it is where I can make a greater contribution to AI and Web3.

For now, thank you, Binance, for five remarkable years.

— Kaiser Ng (@kaizng) November 8, 2026

During his tenure, the exchange navigated bull and bear markets, regulatory changes and what Ng described as “Operation Choke Point 2.0.” He also said that he had to work long hours, at times from 8 a.m. until 2 a.m.

He noted one achievement, for instance, as Binance’s finance team evolved from a conventional back-office role to one that proactively provided business ideas and revenue opportunities.

Understand Binance products, business metrics and commercial operations to collaborate more closely with other departments, says Ng.

Read More: CZ Sends $965K to Giggle Academy, Retires Wallet After Meme Coin Chaos

Justin Yek Named as His Successor

Ng said he was giving Justin Yek the job of CFO. Reuters cited Yek as someone with long experience in the finance sector, most recently as vice president of finance for Airwallex. He stated that Binance had been preparing for the change of chairs for a full six months before the recent crypto breach.

It was revealed less than a week after Binance on Oct. 29 admitted to losing $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency. Ng’s resignation came after a “planned” transition, however, according to the exchange, so there is no linked relationship.

Ng Plans New Ventures in AI and Web3

Next, Ng’s next chapter will be multiple projects, not a single business. He specifically mentioned basketball, music, GPUs, robotics, gold and collectibles as areas that interest him.

Through tokenization, he believes he can now weave the reality of these businesses into blockchain networks. For him, this could provide new perspectives for the capabilities of electronic assets and make conventional assets more accessible.

Finally, Ng spoke about how he could make a bigger impact on AI and Web3 as a founder. He opened his new ventures to others who have an interest, implying that his working processes for the next project may have begun already.

Ng expressed his gratitude to Binance’s leadership, staff, regulators and business partners such as BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton and Mastercard in his farewell message. He also pointed to the exchange’s expansion into TradFi assets and AI-powered user interfaces as signs of its continued development.

title: Tornado Cash-Linked Wallet Sells ETH to Buy Zcash on Hyperliquid
summary:
Key Takeaways: In a 20-hour period, a wallet transferred 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid. The ETH was exchanged for 2,959 ZEC, worth approximately
The post Tornado Cash-Linked Wallet Sells ETH to Buy Zcash on Hyperliquid appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • In a 20-hour period, a wallet transferred 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid.
  • The ETH was exchanged for 2,959 ZEC, worth approximately $3.73 million at the time of the acquisition.
  • Lookonchain noted the transaction, while Arkham noted the ETH-to-ZEC activity.

According to Lookonchain, an onchain wallet turned around about $3.73 million of Ethereum from Tornado Cash to Hyperliquid and then cashed it out for Zcash. This activity compares 1,670 ETH and 2,959 ZEC have been bought in 20 hours.

This is an interesting transaction as the wallet is more than just a tool to transfer funds between platforms. Rather, it sold a good amount of ETH and made use of the proceeds to construct its collections of ZEC.

  • 1,670 ETH Deposited and Sold on Hyperliquid
  • Arkham Tracks the ETH-to-ZEC Activity
    • ZEC Becomes the Destination for the $3.73M ETH Sale

1,670 ETH Deposited and Sold on Hyperliquid

Over the last 20 hours, 1,670 ETH valued at around $3.73 million has been staked on Hyperliquid using Tornado Cash, says Lookonchain in a post on X. The money was then used to buy ZEC. Lookonchain reported that it acquired the total sum of 2,959 ZEC which translates to the equivalent of around $3.73 million.

It appears the hacker is selling ETH to buy ZEC!

Over the past 20 hours, 1,670 $ETH ($3.73M) from #TornadoCash was deposited into Hyperliquid and sold to buy 2,959 $ZEC ($3.73M).

https://t.co/XDlBb5fGSv https://t.co/y2lW20A6bn

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 8, 2026

These are direct Ethereum-to-Zcash conversions. Instead of withdrawing ETH from the mixer and storing it in the wallet, the wallet has handled the funds on Hyperliquid to swap them for another cryptocurrency.

The corresponding number of 1670 ETH was transferred from Tornado Cash, and 2959 ZEC was then purchased via the respective trades that are reported.

Read More: ICE Partners With Trade[XYZ] to Bring $650B Hyperliquid Futures Market to the U.S.

Arkham Tracks the ETH-to-ZEC Activity

Lookonchain also shared an Arkham entity link associated with the activity, labeled ETH-to-ZEC. The tracking page provides an additional reference for examining the wallet’s onchain movements.

Another Arkham entity link pertaining to the activity is ETH-to-ZEC which it was also looking at. The tracking pages are additional references to analyse the onchain tracking of the wallet.

The price of around $3.73 million on both sides of the trade is stated by Lookonchain. As stated, these are reported transaction values and not intended to be an indication that the wallet still contains the same amount of ZEC.

The use of Tornado Cash is also pertinent information to be traced but is not enough to conclude the staking of the assets or even determine who is the owner of the wallet.

ZEC Becomes the Destination for the $3.73M ETH Sale

The big change is that the wallet gave away 1670 ETH and exchanged for 2959 ZEC in the 20-intraday trading period. This isn’t just a simple transfer between wallets, but a substantial conversion from ETH to ZEC.

It was a fraud where hackers sell some ETH coins to acquire some ZEC by virtue of their activities, Lookonchain said. The transaction information, however, only confirms the movement and reported swap, not who owns the wallet or what the origin of the funds are apart from the connection to Tornado Cash.

title: $106M Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity, Solana MEV Bot King Drained for Another $786K
summary:
Key Takeaways: An anonymous EU firm could have lost over $106 million in various exchanges. The suspected attacker transferred USDC and USDT into ETH and XMR and cross-chain. Another Solana
The post $106M Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity, Solana MEV Bot King Drained for Another $786K appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • An anonymous EU firm could have lost over $106 million in various exchanges.
  • The suspected attacker transferred USDC and USDT into ETH and XMR and cross-chain.
  • Another Solana arbitrage bot known as King was singled out and slashed for approximately $786,000.

Crypto investigators continue to monitor two huge security breaches, totaling over $106 million in suspected stolen funds and another $786,000 worth of funds drained from an aging Solana trading bot.

The bigger case is still open but the victim and the exchanges and attacker still were not identified.

  • EU Entity May Have Lost Over $106M in Crypto
  • ZachXBT Rules Out Lazarus Group
    • Stolen Funds Move Beyond Freezable Stablecoins
    • Solana MEV Bot King Loses Another $786K

EU Entity May Have Lost Over $106M in Crypto

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT said an unnamed EU entity is suspected of losing more than $106 million from accounts held at several centralized crypto exchanges on Nov. 1.

Presumptive stolen funds were siphoned off at first in terms of USDC and USDT. ZachXBT released 11 addresses that were associated with the activity, but did not disclose any of the victims or how exchange accounts were opened.

The operant suspected attacker then rapidly reconfigured the asset trail during the next 24-hours.

In addition to USDC being swapped into ether, there were also funds transferred via instant exchange platforms like WellWallet and Kyrrex. Using Wagyu some assets were converted into privacy coin Monero, other assets moved over several blockchain networks.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

ZachXBT Rules Out Lazarus Group

The laundering activity does not seem to follow one of the patterns seen with the North Korea-related Lazarus Group, ZachXBT further said. Although who did the actual theft has not been determined, he said he had a “high degree of confidence” that it was not made by Lazarus.”

The particular is significant, as it comes after the big cyber breakout of cryptocurrencies occurred recently and brought North Korean cyber gangs back into the spotlight. There is, however, no evidence of the EU incident being related to those operations at the moment.

Stolen Funds Move Beyond Freezable Stablecoins

The transition towards stablecoins to ETH and XMR might hinder recoveries. The USDC/USDT issuers are able to freeze tokens on certain addresses; assets like Ether do not have a centralized issuer with similar capabilities. Monero poses yet another challenge as the Privacy features of the platform strip all the details away from transactions.

The speed of using instant exchanges and cross-chain bridges also makes the money trail more complex, allowing investigators to trace activity through various networks and services.

The EU firm in question and the exchanges in question have not confirmed this lack of funds.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Solana MEV Bot King Loses Another $786K

Another incident struck older Solana arbiter King, one of the network’s automated trading bots. Onchain Lens stated that the bot lost approximately $786,000, comprising approximately 4,260 WSOL, 191 SOL and $366,000 worth of stablecoins. Prior to the incident, King had reported to have made about $7.2 million in lifetime profits.

SOLANA MEV BOT KING DRAINED OF $786K 💀

King, one of Solana’s oldest arbitrage bots with $7.2M in lifetime PnL, was drained of ~$786K, including 4.26K $WSOL, 191 $SOL and $366K in stablecoins.

— Onchain Lens (@OnchainLens) November 2, 2026

Onchain Lens was also able to locate the suspect drainer wallet, forward wallet, and the victim wallet’s address. It’s not yet been revealed what specific way was used to access the monitoring account and if the wallet was compromised through this or a different means.
